title.zh: 卷二百四十三 列傳第一百三十一 趙南星 鄒元標 孫慎行 高攀龍 馮從吾
title.en: Volume 243 Biographies 131: Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, Sun Shenxing, Gao Panlong, Feng Congwu
title.raw: 卷二百四十三 列傳第一百三十一 趙南星 鄒元標 孫慎行 高攀龍 馮從吾 Volume 243 Biographies 131: Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, Sun Shenxing, Gao Panlong, Feng Congwu

sentences.zh: 趙南星鄒元標孫慎行

translations.literal: Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, Sun Shenxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, and Sun Shenxing.

translations.literal: Opening bracket 〈 marking an intercalated biography.

sentences.zh: （盛以弘）〉

translations.literal: (Sheng Yihong)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Sheng Yihong)〉

sentences.zh: 高攀龍馮從吾

translations.literal: Gao Panlong, Feng Congwu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Panlong and Feng Congwu.

sentences.zh: 趙南星，字夢白，高邑人。

translations.literal: Zhao Nanxing, styled Mengbai, was a man of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nanxing, whose style name was Mengbai, came from Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除汝寧推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Runing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor in Runing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治行廉平，稍遷戶部主事。

translations.literal: His administration was incorrupt and equitable; he was gradually promoted to Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct in office was upright and fair, and he was gradually promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 張居正寢疾，朝士群禱，南星與顧憲成、姜士昌戒弗往。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng lay ill, court officials prayed in groups; Nanxing, with Gu Xiancheng and Jiang Shichang, admonished against going.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng took to his sickbed, officials thronged the court to pray for him; Nanxing, together with Gu Xiancheng and Jiang Shichang, urged their colleagues not to go.

sentences.zh: 居正歿，調吏部考功。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, he was transferred to Personnel Evaluation in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death he was transferred to the Directorate of Personnel Evaluation in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸。

translations.literal: He resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 起歷文選員外郎。

translations.literal: Recalled, he served successively as Vice Director in the Directorate of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to office, he rose through posts in the Directorate of Appointments, ending as vice director.

sentences.zh: 疏陳天下四大害，言：「楊巍乞休，左都御史吳時來謀代之，忌戶部尚書宋糸熏聲望，連疏排擠。

translations.literal: He memorialized, setting forth the four great harms under Heaven, saying: "Yang Wei has asked to retire; the Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai schemes to replace him, envies the renown of the Minister of Revenue Song Xu, and has sent successive memorials to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he laid out the four great afflictions plaguing the realm, writing: "Yang Wei has asked to retire, yet the left censor-in-chief Wu Shilai is plotting to succeed him. Jealous of Revenue Minister Song Xu's standing, he has peppered the throne with memorials meant to force him out.

sentences.zh: 副都御史詹仰庇力謀吏、兵二部侍郎。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yangbi strenuously schemes for the vice-ministerships of the Ministries of Personnel and War.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Zhan Yangbi is working just as hard to secure the vice-ministerships of Personnel and War.

sentences.zh: 大臣如此，何以責小臣，是謂幹進之害。

translations.literal: When great ministers act thus, how can one demand better of lesser officials? This is what I call the harm of scrambling for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When senior ministers behave this way, how can one hold junior officials to account? This is the harm of unseemly ambition for office.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書沈鯉、侍郎張位、諭德吳中行、南京太仆卿沈思孝相繼自免，獨南京禮部侍郎趙用賢在，詞臣黃洪憲輩每陰讒之，言官唐堯欽、孫愈賢、蔡系周復顯為詆誣。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites Shen Li, Vice Minister Zhang Wei, Tutor Wu Zhongxing, and the Nanjing Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Shen Sixiao resigned one after another; only the Nanjing Vice Minister of Rites Zhao Yongxian remained. Literary officials such as Huang Hongxian constantly slandered him in secret, while remonstrance officials Tang Yaoqin, Sun Yuxian, and Cai Jizhou openly vilified him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Shen Li, Vice Minister Zhang Wei, tutor Wu Zhongxing, and Nanjing director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Shen Sixiao resigned in succession, while only Nanjing vice minister of rites Zhao Yongxian held on. Literary officials such as Huang Hongxian whispered against him behind the scenes, and remonstrance officials Tang Yaoqin, Sun Yuxian, and Cai Jizhou joined in open defamation.

sentences.zh: 眾正不容，宵人得誌，是謂傾危之害。

translations.literal: The upright cannot be tolerated while petty men have their way—this is what I call the harm of overturning the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the upright have no room to stand and schemers carry the day, the polity itself is put at risk—this is the harm of subverting good government.

sentences.zh: 州縣長吏選授太輕，部寺之官計日而取郡守，不問才行。

translations.literal: The selection and appointment of prefectural and county chiefs is far too lax; officials of ministries and directorates count the days until they may take up posts as prefects, without asking about talent or conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments to prefectural and county magistracies are made far too lightly; officials in the central ministries and directorates treat a provincial post as something to be seized on a timetable, with no regard for ability or character.

sentences.zh: 而撫按論人贓私有據，不曰未甚，則曰任淺，概止降調，其意以為惜才，不知此乃惜不才也。

translations.literal: Yet when grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners discuss officials' proven corruption, they either say it was not grave or that tenure was brief, and generally stop at demotion and transfer, thinking thereby to cherish talent—not knowing that this is cherishing the untalented.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial overseers report proven corruption, the response is either "not very serious" or "too short a tenure," and the offender is usually merely demoted and reassigned. They imagine they are sparing talent; in truth they are sparing the talentless.

sentences.zh: 吏治日汙，民生日瘁，是謂州縣之害。

translations.literal: Officialdom grows daily more filthy and the people's livelihood daily more wretched—this is what I call the harm of the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: As local administration rots, the common people grow poorer by the day—this is the harm wrought at the prefectural and county level.

sentences.zh: 鄉官之權大於守令，橫行無忌，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: The power of local gentry exceeds that of magistrates; they run rampant without restraint, and none dares call them to account.
translations.idiomatic: Rural gentry now wield more power than the magistrates themselves, riding roughshod over the countryside with no one daring to check them.

sentences.zh: 如渭南知縣張棟，治行無雙，裁抑鄉官，被讒不獲行取，是謂鄉官之害。

translations.literal: The magistrate Zhang Dong of Weinan, whose administration was without peer, curbed the local gentry and, slandered for it, was denied selection for capital office—this is what I call the harm of local gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dong, magistrate of Weinan, governed with unrivaled integrity and reined in the local gentry; for that he was slandered and blocked from promotion to the capital—this is the harm of entrenched rural power.

sentences.zh: 四害不除，天下不可得治。

translations.literal: Unless these four harms are removed, the realm cannot be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Until these four scourges are cleared away, the realm cannot be well governed.

sentences.zh: 」疏出，朝論韙之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was issued, court opinion approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial appeared, opinion at court broadly approved it.

sentences.zh: 而中所抨擊悉時相所庇，於是給事中李春開起而駁之。

translations.literal: Yet those he attacked were all under the protection of the chief ministers of the day, and so Supervising Secretary Li Chunkai rose to rebut him.
translations.idiomatic: But nearly everyone he named enjoyed the chief ministers' protection, and supervising secretary Li Chunkai rose to refute him.

sentences.zh: 其疏先下，南星幾獲譴。

translations.literal: Chunkai's memorial was issued first, and Nanxing nearly suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chunkai's memorial reached the throne first, and Nanxing came close to being punished.

sentences.zh: 給事中王繼光、史孟麟、萬自約，部曹姜士昌、吳正誌並助南星詆春開，且發時來、仰庇、洪憲讒諂狀。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Wang Jiguang, Shi Menglin, and Wan Ziyue, together with section officials Jiang Shichang and Wu Zhengzhi, all aided Nanxing in denouncing Chunkai and exposed the slanderous flattery of Shilai, Yangbi, and Hongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Wang Jiguang, Shi Menglin, and Wan Ziyue, together with section officials Jiang Shichang and Wu Zhengzhi, rallied to Nanxing's side against Chunkai and laid bare the slander and flattery of Shilai, Yangbi, and Hongxian.

sentences.zh: 春開氣沮，然南星卒以病歸。

translations.literal: Chunkai's spirit was damped, yet Nanxing still ended by returning home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Chunkai lost heart, but Nanxing still retired in the end, again citing illness.

sentences.zh: 再起，歷考功郎中。

translations.literal: Recalled again, he served successively as Director in the Directorate of Personnel Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned back once more, he served as director in the Directorate of Personnel Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 二十一年大計京官，與尚書孫鑨秉公澄汰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year came the general review of capital officials; together with Minister Sun Lu he conducted a fair purge.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Wanli came the great triennial review of capital officials, which he conducted impartially with Minister Sun Lu.

sentences.zh: 首黜所親都給事中王三余及鑨甥文選員外郎呂胤昌，他附麗政府及大學士趙誌臯弟皆不免，政府大不堪。

translations.literal: He first demoted his own kinsman, Chief Supervising Secretary Wang Sanyu, and Lu's nephew, Vice Director of Appointments Lü Yinchang; others who clung to the government faction and even the younger brother of Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao were not spared, and the government was deeply affronted.
translations.idiomatic: He began by demoting his own relative, chief supervising secretary Wang Sanyu, and Lu's nephew Lü Yinchang, vice director of appointments; others who had attached themselves to the ruling faction, down to Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao's younger brother, were struck as well, and the court faction was deeply stung.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉道隆因劾吏部議留拾遺庶僚非法。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Daolong thereupon impeached the Ministry of Personnel for illegally retaining remonstrance officials and junior staff.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Liu Daolong then impeached the ministry for unlawfully retaining remonstrance officials and junior appointees.

sentences.zh: 得旨，南星等專權植黨，貶三官。

translations.literal: An edict followed: Nanxing and the others were monopolizing power and planting factions; three officials were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied that Nanxing and his colleagues had monopolized power and formed factions; three officials were demoted.

sentences.zh: 俄因李世達等疏救，斥南星為民。

translations.literal: Soon, because Li Shida and others memorialized in their defense, Nanxing was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, after Li Shida and others pleaded for them, Nanxing was stripped of rank and sent home as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 後論救者悉被譴，鑨亦去位，一時善類幾空。

translations.literal: Later, all who pleaded for them were punished; Lu also left office, and for a time worthy men were nearly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Those who later spoke up for them were punished in turn; Lu left his post as well, and for a time the ranks of the upright were nearly emptied.

sentences.zh: 事具鑨傳。

translations.literal: The affair is set forth in Lu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recounted in Sun Lu's biography.

sentences.zh: 南星裏居，名益高，與鄒元標、顧憲成，海內擬之「三君」。

translations.literal: Living in retirement, Nanxing's fame grew ever higher; with Zou Yuanbiao and Gu Xiancheng he was styled by the empire the "Three Lords."
translations.idiomatic: In retirement his reputation only grew; together with Zou Yuanbiao and Gu Xiancheng he was hailed throughout the realm as one of the "Three Lords."

sentences.zh: 中外論薦者百十疏，卒不起。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court more than a hundred memorials recommended him, yet in the end he was not recalled.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred memorials from within and beyond the court urged his recall, yet he was never brought back.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, Nanxing was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Nanxing was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 俄改右通政，進太常卿，至則擢工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Right Commissioner of the Court for the Imperial Clan, advanced to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and upon arrival was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made right commissioner of the Court for the Imperial Clan, then minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; no sooner had he arrived than he was promoted vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 居數月，拜左都御史，慨然以整齊天下為任。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief and vowed to set the realm in order.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was named left censor-in-chief and took upon himself the task of putting the government to rights.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年大計京官，以故給事中亓詩教、趙興邦、官應震、吳亮嗣先朝結黨亂政，議黜之，吏科都給事中魏應嘉力持不可。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi came the general review of capital officials; because the former supervising secretaries Qi Shijiao, Zhao Xingbang, Guan Yingzhen, and Wu Liangsi had formed factions and disturbed government in the previous reign, he proposed their dismissal, but the Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section Wei Yingjia strenuously objected.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianqi, during the great review of capital officials, he moved to dismiss the former supervising secretaries Qi Shijiao, Zhao Xingbang, Guan Yingzhen, and Wu Liangsi for the factional disorder they had sown late in the previous reign; Wei Yingjia, chief supervising secretary of the personnel section, fought the decision hard.

sentences.zh: 南星著《四兇論》，卒與考功郎程正己置四人不謹。

translations.literal: Nanxing wrote the 《Treatise on the Four Villains》 and, with Evaluation Director Cheng Zhengji, finally placed the four men in the "not diligent" category.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing wrote his 《Treatise on the Four Villains》 and, with evaluation director Cheng Zhengji, finally marked all four as "not diligent."

sentences.zh: 他所澄汰，一如為考功時。

translations.literal: His other purges followed the same standard as when he had served in Personnel Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of his purge followed the same uncompromising standard he had shown in the directorate of evaluation.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡按張素養薦部內人材，及姚宗文、邵輔忠、劉廷元，南星劾其謬，素養坐奪俸。

translations.literal: The touring censor of Zhejiang Zhang Suyang recommended men of talent within his jurisdiction, including Yao Zongwen, Shao Fuzhong, and Liu Tingyuan; Nanxing impeached the recommendation as improper and Suyang was fined one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suyang, the touring censor of Zhejiang, recommended several men from his circuit, among them Yao Zongwen, Shao Fuzhong, and Liu Tingyuan; Nanxing attacked the list as improper and Suyang was fined a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 先是，巡方者有提薦之例，南星已奏止之；

translations.literal: Earlier, touring officials had had a practice of submitting recommendations; Nanxing had already memorialized to stop it;
translations.idiomatic: Touring censors had long enjoyed the custom of forwarding talent lists; Nanxing had already secured an order ending the practice;

sentences.zh: 而陜西高弘圖、山西徐揚先、宣大李思啟、河東劉大受，復踵行如故，南星並劾奏之，巡方者始知畏法。

translations.literal: yet Gao Hongtu in Shaanxi, Xu Yangxian in Shanxi, Li Siqi in Xuan-Da, and Liu Dashou in Hedong all followed the old ways as before, and Nanxing impeached them together, so that touring officials at last learned to fear the law.
translations.idiomatic: yet Gao Hongtu in Shaanxi, Xu Yangxian in Shanxi, Li Siqi in Xuan-Da, and Liu Dashou in Hedong all did the same as before, and Nanxing impeached them together until touring officials at last learned to fear the law.

sentences.zh: 尋代張問達為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Zhang Wenda as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon succeeded Zhang Wenda as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 當是時，人務奔競，苞苴恣行，言路橫尤甚。

translations.literal: At that time men strove only for advancement; gift-giving ran wild, and the remonstrance circuit was especially overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Men at court cared for nothing but advancement; bribery ran unchecked, and the remonstrance offices were more overbearing than ever.

sentences.zh: 每文選郎出，輒邀之半道，為人求官，不得則加以惡聲，或逐之去。

translations.literal: Whenever a director of appointments went out, he would be waylaid halfway and pressed to secure posts for others; if he refused, they would heap abuse on him or even drive him away.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a director of appointments stepped outside, someone would intercept him on the road to beg an appointment; refusal brought abuse, and sometimes he was driven off outright.

sentences.zh: 選郎即公正無如何，尚書亦太息而已。

translations.literal: Even when the director was upright there was nothing to be done; the minister could only sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Even an upright director was helpless, and the minister could only sigh.

sentences.zh: 南星素疾其弊，銳意澄清，獨行己誌，政府及中貴亦不得有所幹請，諸人憚其剛嚴不敢犯。

translations.literal: Nanxing had long detested these abuses and was determined to cleanse them, going his own way; neither the government nor the inner eunuchs could obtain requests from him, and all feared his stern rigor and did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing had long hated these abuses and set out to purge them, following his own course; neither the cabinet nor the inner eunuchs could secure favors from him, and men feared his severity too much to test him.

sentences.zh: 有給事為貲郎求鹽運司，即註貲郎王府，而出給事於外。

translations.literal: A supervising secretary sought a salt-transport post for his son-in-law, who was a tribute student; Nanxing registered the son-in-law for service in a princely establishment and sent the supervising secretary abroad.
translations.idiomatic: One supervising secretary sought a salt-transport commission for his son-in-law, a tribute student; Nanxing posted the son-in-law to a prince's household and sent the father out of the capital on assignment.

sentences.zh: 知縣石三畏素貪，夤緣將行取，南星亦置之王府。

translations.literal: The magistrate Shi Sanwei had long been greedy and, by pull, was about to be selected for capital office; Nanxing likewise assigned him to a princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate Shi Sanwei was notoriously corrupt and, through connections, was on the verge of capital promotion; Nanxing assigned him to a prince's household as well.

sentences.zh: 時進士無為王官者，南星不恤也。

translations.literal: At the time no jinshi served as a prince's official; Nanxing paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: No jinshi had served in a prince's household in living memory; Nanxing did not care.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢雅重之，嘗於帝前稱其任事。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian held him in high regard and once praised his diligence before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian thought highly of him and once praised his diligence before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 一日，遣娣子傅應星介一中書贄見，南星麾之去。

translations.literal: One day he sent his brother's son Fu Yingxing, bearing a visiting card from a palace secretary, to call on him; Nanxing drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: One day he sent his nephew Fu Yingxing, carrying a visiting card from a palace secretary, to call on Nanxing, who showed him the door.

sentences.zh: 嘗並坐弘政門，選通政司參議，正色語忠賢曰：「主上沖齡，我輩內外臣子宜各努力為善。

translations.literal: Once, sitting together at Hongzheng Gate while selecting a vice commissioner of the Court for the Imperial Clan, he said gravely to Zhongxian: "The sovereign is still young; we inner and outer ministers ought each to strive to do good."
translations.idiomatic: Once, as they sat together at Hongzheng Gate selecting a vice commissioner of the Court for the Imperial Clan, he said gravely to Zhongxian: "The sovereign is still a child; we ministers inside and outside ought each to do our utmost for the good."

sentences.zh: 」忠賢默然，怒形於色。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was silent, anger showing on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian said nothing, but anger showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 大學士魏廣微，南星友允貞子也，素以通家子畜之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wei Guangwei was the son of Nanxing's friend Wei Yunzhen, and he had long treated him as a son of the household.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wei Guangwei was the son of Nanxing's friend Wei Yunzhen, whom Nanxing had long treated as a member of the family.

sentences.zh: 廣微入內閣，嘗三至南星門，拒勿見。

translations.literal: After Guangwei entered the Grand Secretariat he called three times at Nanxing's door and was refused each time.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangwei entered the Grand Secretariat he called three times at Nanxing's door and was turned away each time.

sentences.zh: 又嘗嘆曰：「見泉無子。

translations.literal: He also once sighed: "Jianquan left no worthy son."
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing once sighed aloud: "Jianquan left no worthy son."

sentences.zh: 」見泉，允貞別號也。

translations.literal: Jianquan was Yunzhen's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Jianquan was Wei Yunzhen's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 廣微恨刺骨，與忠賢比而龁南星。

translations.literal: Guangwei hated him to the bone and joined Zhongxian in gnawing at Nanxing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei hated him to the marrow and joined Zhongxian in working to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 東林勢盛，眾正盈朝。

translations.literal: The Donglin faction was in the ascendant and upright men filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Donglin movement was ascendant and the upright filled the court.

sentences.zh: 南星益搜舉遺佚，布之庶位。

translations.literal: Nanxing all the more sought out overlooked men of talent and placed them in subordinate posts.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing searched out overlooked talent all the more eagerly and placed such men in secondary posts throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 高攀龍、楊漣、左光鬥秉憲；

translations.literal: Gao Panlong, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou held the censorate;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Panlong, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou held the censorate;

sentences.zh: 李騰芳、陳於廷佐銓；

translations.literal: Li Tengfang and Chen Yuting assisted in appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Li Tengfang and Chen Yuting assisted with appointments;

sentences.zh: 魏大中、袁化中長科道；

translations.literal: Wei Dazhong and Yuan Huazhong headed the remonstrance offices;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dazhong and Yuan Huazhong led the remonstrance offices;

sentences.zh: 鄭三俊、李邦華、孫居相、饒伸、王之寀輩悉置卿貳。

translations.literal: Zheng Sanjun, Li Banghua, Sun Juxiang, Rao Shen, Wang Zhicai, and others were all placed in vice-ministerial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun, Li Banghua, Sun Juxiang, Rao Shen, Wang Zhicai, and others were all given vice-ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 而四司之屬，鄒維璉、夏嘉遇、張光前、程國祥、劉廷諫亦皆民譽。

translations.literal: Among the four directorates as well, Zou Weilian, Xia Jiayu, Zhang Guangqian, Cheng Guoxiang, and Liu Tingjian enjoyed the people's praise.
translations.idiomatic: Among the four bureaus of the ministry, Zou Weilian, Xia Jiayu, Zhang Guangqian, Cheng Guoxiang, and Liu Tingjian likewise enjoyed public esteem.

sentences.zh: 中外忻忻望治，而小人側目，滋欲去南星。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court rejoiced in hope of good government, while petty men glared sideways and all the more wished Nanxing gone.
translations.idiomatic: Within and beyond the court men looked forward to better days, while petty officials glared and longed all the more to see Nanxing removed.

sentences.zh: 給事中傅櫆以維璉改吏部己不與聞，首假汪文言發難，劾南星紊舊制，植私人。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Fu Zhen, because he had not been consulted when Weilian was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, first used Wang Wenyan as a pretext to attack, impeaching Nanxing for disordering old regulations and planting private followers.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Fu Zhen, angry that he had not been consulted when Weilian was moved to personnel, opened the attack through Wang Wenyan, impeaching Nanxing for violating established procedure and filling posts with his own men.

sentences.zh: 維璉引去，南星奏留之，小人愈恨。

translations.literal: Weilian withdrew; Nanxing memorialized to retain him, and the petty men hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian offered to withdraw; Nanxing memorialized to keep him, and the malcontents hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 會漣劾忠賢疏上，宮府益水火。

translations.literal: When Lian's memorial impeaching Zhongxian went up, palace and government became all the more like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian's memorial impeaching Zhongxian reached the throne, court and palace grew more bitterly opposed than ever.

sentences.zh: 南星遂杜門乞休，不許。

translations.literal: Nanxing thereupon shut his door and begged to retire, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing shut his doors and asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 攀龍之劾崔呈秀也，南星議戍之。

translations.literal: When Panlong impeached Cui Chengxiu, Nanxing proposed banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Panlong impeached Cui Chengxiu, Nanxing proposed that he be banished.

sentences.zh: 呈秀窘，夜走忠賢邸，叩頭乞哀，言：「不去南星及攀龍、漣等，我兩人未知死所。

translations.literal: Chengxiu was cornered; by night he ran to Zhongxian's residence, kowtowed, and begged for mercy, saying: "Unless Nanxing and Panlong, Lian, and the others are removed, the two of us do not know where we shall die."
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Chengxiu fled by night to Zhongxian's house, kowtowed, and pleaded: "Unless Nanxing and Panlong, Lian, and the rest are removed, neither of us knows where we shall end our days."

sentences.zh: 」忠賢大以為然，遂與定謀。

translations.literal: Zhongxian greatly agreed and thereupon joined in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was fully persuaded, and together they laid their plan.

sentences.zh: 會山西缺巡撫，河南布政使郭尚友求之。

translations.literal: When the post of grand coordinator of Shanxi fell vacant, Guo Shangyou, administrative commissioner of Henan, sought it.
translations.idiomatic: A vacancy opened for grand coordinator of Shanxi, and Guo Shangyou, administrative commissioner of Henan, sought the post.

sentences.zh: 南星以太常卿謝應祥有清望，首列以請。

translations.literal: Nanxing, because Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xie Yingxiang enjoyed a reputation for integrity, listed him first in the nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing, holding Vice Minister Xie Yingxiang of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in high regard for his integrity, placed his name first on the nomination.

sentences.zh: 既得旨，而御史陳九疇受廣微指，言應祥嘗知嘉善，大中出其門，大中以師故，謀於文選郎嘉遇而用之，徇私當斥。

translations.literal: After the edict was issued, Censor Chen Jiuchou, acting on Guangwei's instructions, said that Yingxiang had once served as magistrate of Jiashan, that Dazhong had been his student, and that Dazhong, because of this teacher-student tie, had plotted with the Director of Appointments Jiayu to secure the appointment—favoritism that called for dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Once the appointment was approved, censor Chen Jiuchou, acting at Guangwei's direction, charged that Yingxiang had once been magistrate of Jiashan, that Dazhong had been his pupil, and that Dazhong, out of regard for his teacher, had conspired with appointments director Jiayu to secure the post—nepotism that demanded punishment.

sentences.zh: 大中、嘉遇疏辯，語侵九疇，九疇再疏力詆，並下部議。

translations.literal: Dazhong and Jiayu memorialized in defense, their words impugning Jiuchou; Jiuchou memorialized again, vehemently denouncing them, and the matter was sent down for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong and Jiayu defended themselves in memorials that reflected on Jiuchou; Jiuchou answered with another fierce attack, and the case was sent to the ministries for joint review.

sentences.zh: 南星、攀龍極言應祥以人望推舉，大中、嘉遇無私，九疇妄言不可聽。

translations.literal: Nanxing and Panlong strongly argued that Yingxiang had been nominated for his public standing, that Dazhong and Jiayu were without private motive, and that Jiuchou's reckless words should not be heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing and Panlong insisted that Yingxiang had been put forward on merit, that Dazhong and Jiayu were blameless, and that Jiuchou's charges were not to be credited.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大怒，矯旨黜大中、嘉遇，並黜九疇，而責南星等朋謀結黨。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was furious and forged an edict dismissing Dazhong and Jiayu and also dismissing Jiuchou, while rebuking Nanxing and the others for factional conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was enraged and forged an edict dismissing Dazhong and Jiayu—and Jiuchou as well—while rebuking Nanxing and his allies for forming a faction.

sentences.zh: 南星遽引罪求去，忠賢復矯旨切責，放歸。

translations.literal: Nanxing hastily took blame and asked to leave; Zhongxian again forged an edict sharply reproving him and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing at once took the blame and asked to withdraw; Zhongxian forged another edict sharply reproving him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 明日，攀龍亦引去。

translations.literal: The next day Panlong also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Panlong resigned as well.

sentences.zh: 給事中沈惟炳論救，亦出之外。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Shen Weibing pleaded in their defense and was also sent abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Shen Weibing spoke up for them and was sent out of the capital too.

sentences.zh: 俄以會推忤忠賢意，並斥於廷、漣、光鬥、化中，引南星所擯徐兆魁、喬應甲、王紹徽等置要地。

translations.literal: Soon, because the court nomination displeased Zhongxian, Bing Yu, Lian, Guangdou, and Huazhong were expelled together, and men Nanxing had rejected—Xu Zhaokui, Qiao Yingjia, Wang Shaohui, and others—were placed in key posts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when a court nomination displeased Zhongxian, Bing Yu, Lian, Guangdou, and Huazhong were driven out together, while men Nanxing had cast aside—Xu Zhaokui, Qiao Yingjia, Wang Shaohui, and the like—were installed in crucial posts.

sentences.zh: 小人競進，天下大柄盡歸忠賢矣。

translations.literal: Petty men vied for advancement, and the great lever of the realm passed wholly into Zhongxian's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men rushed forward, and the great lever of state fell entirely into Zhongxian's hands.

sentences.zh: 忠賢及其黨惡南星甚，每矯敕諭，必目為元兇。

translations.literal: Zhongxian and his faction hated Nanxing deeply; whenever they forged edicts of instruction they invariably styled him the arch-villain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian and his faction hated Nanxing with a passion; every forged instruction branded him the arch-villain.

sentences.zh: 於是御史張訥劾南星十大罪，並劾維璉、國祥、嘉遇及王允成。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor Zhang Na impeached Nanxing on ten great crimes, and also impeached Weilian, Guoxiang, Jiayu, and Wang Yuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Na then impeached Nanxing on ten capital charges and attacked Weilian, Guoxiang, Jiayu, and Wang Yuncheng as well.

sentences.zh: 得旨，並削籍。

translations.literal: An edict followed: all were struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The forged edict followed: all were struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 令再奏南星私黨，訥復列上邦華及孫鼎相等十四人，並貶黜。

translations.literal: They were ordered to memorialize again on Nanxing's private faction; Na again listed Banghua and Sun Dingxiang and fourteen others, who were all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: They were told to submit a further list of Nanxing's partisans; Na named Banghua, Sun Dingxiang, and fourteen others, who were demoted in turn.

sentences.zh: 自是為南星擯棄者，無不拔擢，其素所推獎者，率遭奇禍。

translations.literal: Henceforth those Nanxing had cast aside were all promoted, while those he had commended mostly met with strange calamities.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, men Nanxing had rejected were advanced one after another, while those he had favored mostly met with bizarre misfortune.

sentences.zh: 諸幹進速化之徒，一擊南星，輒遂所欲。

translations.literal: Men who scrambled for quick advancement had only to strike at Nanxing to gain their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who wanted rapid promotion had only to strike at Nanxing to get his wish.

sentences.zh: 而石三畏亦起為御史，疏攻南星及李三才、顧憲成、孫丕揚、王圖等十五人。

translations.literal: Shi Sanwei also rose to be censor and memorialized attacking Nanxing together with Li Sancai, Gu Xiancheng, Sun Piyang, Wang Tu, and fifteen others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sanwei, too, was raised to censor and memorialized against Nanxing along with Li Sancai, Gu Xiancheng, Sun Piyang, Wang Tu, and fifteen others.

sentences.zh: 死者皆削奪，縉紳禍益烈。

translations.literal: Those who had died were all posthumously stripped of honors, and calamity among the gentry grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The dead among them were posthumously stripped of honors, and disaster among the gentry grew ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 尋以汪文言獄詞連及南星，下撫按提問。

translations.literal: Soon, through the case testimony of Wang Wenyan, Nanxing was implicated; he was sent down to the grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the testimony in Wang Wenyan's case implicated Nanxing, and he was sent down to the provincial authorities for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 適郭尚友巡撫保定，而巡按馬逢臯亦憾南星，乃相與庭辱之。

translations.literal: It happened that Guo Shangyou was grand coordinator of Baoding and Surveillance Commissioner Ma Fenggao also bore a grudge against Nanxing; the two together humiliated him in open court.
translations.idiomatic: By chance Guo Shangyou was grand coordinator of Baoding and surveillance commissioner Ma Fenggao also resented Nanxing; together they shamed him in open session.

sentences.zh: 笞其子清衡及外孫王鐘龐，系之獄，坐南星贓萬五千。

translations.literal: They flogged his son Qingheng and grandsons Wang and Zhongpang, imprisoned them, and convicted Nanxing of fifteen thousand taels in illicit gains.
translations.idiomatic: They beat his son Qingheng and grandsons Wang and Zhongpang, threw them into prison, and convicted Nanxing of embezzling fifteen thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 南星家素貧，親故捐助，始獲竣。

translations.literal: Nanxing's family had always been poor; only when kin and friends contributed could the fine be paid.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanxing household had always been poor; relatives and friends had to raise the money before the penalty could be settled.

sentences.zh: 卒戍南星代州，清衡莊浪，鐘龐永昌。

translations.literal: In the end Nanxing was banished to Daizhou, Qingheng to Zhuanglang, and Zhongpang to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing was sent into exile at Daizhou, Qingheng to Zhuanglang, and Zhongpang to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 嫡母馮氏、生母李氏，並哀慟而卒。

translations.literal: His stepmother, Lady Feng, and his birth mother, Lady Li, both died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother Lady Feng and his birth mother Lady Li both died of grief.

sentences.zh: 子生七齡，驚怖死。

translations.literal: A son who was seven sui died of fright.
translations.idiomatic: A son of seven sui died of terror.

sentences.zh: 南星抵戍所，處之怡然。

translations.literal: When Nanxing reached the place of banishment, he bore it with composure.
translations.idiomatic: At the place of exile he bore his lot with composure.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝登極，有詔赦還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie ascended, an edict ordered his recall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne, an edict ordered his recall.

sentences.zh: 巡撫牟誌夔，忠賢黨也，故遲遣之，竟卒於戍所。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Mou Zhikui, a partisan of Zhongxian, deliberately delayed sending him and Nanxing died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Mou Zhikui, a partisan of Zhongxian, deliberately delayed his release, and Nanxing died in exile.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太子太保，謚忠毅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent and given the posthumous name Zhongyi, "Loyal and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 櫆、呈秀、廣微、九疇、兆魁、應甲、紹徽、訥、三畏、尚友、誌夔，俱名麗逆案，為世大僇焉。

translations.literal: Zhen, Chengxiu, Guangwei, Jiuchou, Zhaokui, Yingjia, Shaohui, Na, Sanwei, Shangyou, and Zhikui were all listed in the case of traitors and became objects of universal execration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, Chengxiu, Guangwei, Jiuchou, Zhaokui, Yingjia, Shaohui, Na, Sanwei, Shangyou, and Zhikui were all named in the roll of traitors and became bywords for infamy.

sentences.zh: 鄒元標，字爾瞻，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zou Yuanbiao, styled Erzhan, was a man of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yuanbiao, whose style name was Erzhan, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 九歲通《五經》。

translations.literal: At nine sui he mastered the 《Five Classics》.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of nine he had mastered the 《Five Classics》.

sentences.zh: 泰和胡直，嘉靖中進士，官至福建按察使，師歐陽德、羅洪先，得王守仁之傳。

translations.literal: Hu Zhi of Taihe, a jinshi of the Jiajing reign, rose to Regional Inspector of Fujian; he studied under Ouyang De and Luo Hongxian and received the transmission of Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhi of Taihe, a Jiajing-era jinshi who rose to regional inspector of Fujian, had studied under Ouyang De and Luo Hongxian and inherited Wang Yangming's teaching.

sentences.zh: 元標弱冠從直遊，即有誌為學。

translations.literal: In his weak-crown years Yuanbiao followed Zhi and at once set his heart on learning.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his teens Yuanbiao studied under Hu Zhi and resolved to devote himself to learning.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 觀政刑部。

translations.literal: He observed administration in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served a probationary term in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 張居正奪情，元標抗疏切諫。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng seized mourning leave, Yuanbiao submitted a stern memorial in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng forced his way back to office without completing mourning, Yuanbiao submitted a fierce memorial of opposition.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「陛下以居正有利社稷耶？

translations.literal: He also said: "Does Your Majesty keep Juzheng because he benefits the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Does Your Majesty retain Juzheng because he serves the altars of state?

sentences.zh: 居正才雖可為，學術則偏；

translations.literal: Juzheng's talent may be usable, but his learning is partial;
translations.idiomatic: His talent may be usable, but his learning is one-sided;

sentences.zh: 誌雖欲為，自用太甚。

translations.literal: though his will aims to act, he is far too self-willed.
translations.idiomatic: and though his will is to govern, he is far too self-willed.

sentences.zh: 其設施乖張者，如州縣入學，限以十五六人，有司希指，更損其數。

translations.literal: Among his perverse measures: limiting county and prefectural school enrollment to fifteen or sixteen persons, while local officials, reading his intent, reduced the number still further.
translations.idiomatic: Among his misguided policies: capping enrollment in county and prefectural schools at fifteen or sixteen students, while local officials, eager to please him, cut the quotas still further.

sentences.zh: 是進賢未廣也。

translations.literal: Thus the promotion of worthies has not been broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the path for worthy men to advance has been narrowed, not widened.

sentences.zh: 諸道決囚，亦有定額，所司懼罰，數必取盈。

translations.literal: In deciding capital cases on the circuits there are also fixed quotas; the offices fear punishment and invariably fill the quota to excess.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit judges also face fixed quotas in capital cases; fearing punishment, they invariably fill the quota to excess.

sentences.zh: 是斷刑太濫也。

translations.literal: Thus the infliction of punishment is too lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Thus executions have grown far too lavish.

sentences.zh: 大臣持祿茍容，小臣畏罪緘默，有今日陳言而明日獲譴者。

translations.literal: Great ministers hold their salaries and are content; lesser officials fear crime and keep silent—some speak today and are punished tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers cling to their stipends and hold their tongues; junior officials fear reprisal and stay silent—some who speak today are punished tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 是言路未通也。

translations.literal: Thus the remonstrance circuit is not open.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the channels of remonstrance remain blocked.

sentences.zh: 黃河泛濫為災，民有駕蒿為巢、啜水為餐者，而有司不以聞。

translations.literal: The Yellow River has overflowed in disaster; people ride on artemisia rafts for nests and drink water for meals, yet the offices do not report it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River has burst its banks; people live on reed rafts and drink muddy water for sustenance, yet officials do not report it.

sentences.zh: 是民隱未周也。

translations.literal: Thus the people's hidden suffering is not fully known.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people's hidden suffering never reaches the throne.

sentences.zh: 其他用刻深之吏，沮豪傑之材，又不可枚數矣。

translations.literal: Besides these, harsh officials and the thwarting of heroic talent cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, harsh magistrates and the suppression of able men are too numerous to list.

sentences.zh: 伏讀敕諭『朕學尚未成，誌尚未定，先生既去，前功盡隳』，陛下言及此，宗社無疆之福也。

translations.literal: I have read the edict of instruction, 'My learning is not yet accomplished, my will not yet settled; with the gentleman gone, the earlier achievement is wholly undone'—when Your Majesty speaks thus, the altars of state enjoy boundless blessing.
translations.idiomatic: I have read Your Majesty's instruction: 'My learning is not yet complete, my purpose not yet fixed; with the gentleman gone, all prior effort is undone.' When the throne speaks thus, the realm itself is blessed.

sentences.zh: 雖然，弼成聖學，輔翼聖誌者，未可謂在廷無人也。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, those who complete the sage's learning and assist the sage's will cannot be said to be absent from court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who can complete the sovereign's learning and steady his purpose are not absent from this court.

sentences.zh: 且幸而居正丁艱，猶可挽留；

translations.literal: Moreover, it is fortunate that Juzheng is in mourning and may still be retained;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Juzheng is in mourning and may still be recalled;

sentences.zh: 脫不幸遂捐館舍，陛下之學將終不成，誌將終不定耶？

translations.literal: if by misfortune he should die, will Your Majesty's learning never be accomplished and Your will never settled?
translations.idiomatic: but if he should die, will Your Majesty's learning never be completed and your purpose never fixed?

sentences.zh: 臣觀居正疏言『世有非常之人，然後辦非常之事』，若以奔喪為常事而不屑為者，不知人惟盡此五常之道，然後謂之人。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that in Juzheng's memorial he says, 'Only when the age has an extraordinary man can it accomplish extraordinary things'—yet if one treats rushing home for a parent's funeral as a common matter beneath one's dignity, one does not know that only by fulfilling these five constant relationships is one called human.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng wrote in his memorial that 'only an extraordinary man can accomplish extraordinary things'—yet if one treats a parent's funeral as beneath one's dignity, one forgets that humanity consists in fulfilling the five constant relationships.

sentences.zh: 今有人於此，親生而不顧，親死而不奔，猶自號於世曰我非常人也，世不以為喪心，則以為禽彘，可謂之非常人哉？

translations.literal: Suppose there is one who, while his parent lives, does not care for him, and when his parent dies does not rush home, yet proclaims to the world, 'I am an extraordinary man'—if the world does not call him heartless, it will call him no better than a beast; can such a one be called extraordinary?
translations.idiomatic: If a man neglects his living parent and does not mourn his dead one, yet calls himself extraordinary, the world will deem him heartless or no better than a beast—can that be called extraordinary?

sentences.zh: 」疏就，懷之入朝，適廷杖吳中行等。

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished, he carried it to court; it happened that Wu Zhongxing and others were being beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was ready he carried it to court just as Wu Zhongxing and others were undergoing court beating.

sentences.zh: 元標俟杖畢，取疏授中官，紿曰：「此乞假疏也。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao waited until the beating was over, gave the memorial to a palace attendant, and deceived him, saying, "This is a request for leave."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao waited until the beating ended, handed the memorial to a palace attendant, and said it was merely a leave request.

sentences.zh: 」及入，居正大怒，亦廷杖八十，謫戍都勻衛。

translations.literal: Once he entered, Juzheng was greatly angered and had him beaten eighty strokes at court and banished to Dutun Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, Juzheng was furious and had him beaten eighty strokes at court and banished to Dutun Guard.

sentences.zh: 衛在萬山中，夷獠與居，元標處之怡然。

translations.literal: The guard lay deep in the ten-thousand mountains, where Yi and Liao aborigines dwelt; Yuanbiao lived there with composure.
translations.idiomatic: The guard lay deep in the mountains among Yi and Miao peoples, yet Yuanbiao lived there at ease.

sentences.zh: 益究心理學，學以大進。

translations.literal: He pursued the learning of the mind all the more and made great progress.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the learning of the mind with renewed energy and advanced greatly.

sentences.zh: 巡按禦中承居正指，將害元標。

translations.literal: The touring censor Yu Zhongcheng, acting on Juzheng's instructions, intended to harm Yuanbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Yu Zhongcheng, acting on Juzheng's orders, meant to destroy Yuanbiao.

sentences.zh: 行次鎮遠，一夕，御史暴死。

translations.literal: Passing Zhenyuan, one night the censor died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Zhenyuan, the censor died suddenly one night.

sentences.zh: 元標謫居六年，居正歿，召拜吏科給事中。

translations.literal: After six years in banishment, when Juzheng died Yuanbiao was recalled and appointed Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in exile, when Juzheng died Yuanbiao was recalled as supervising secretary in the personnel section.

sentences.zh: 首陳培聖德、親臣工、肅憲紀、崇儒行、飭撫臣五事。

translations.literal: He first set forth five matters: cultivating sagely virtue, drawing close to ministers, rectifying the statutes, honoring Confucian conduct, and restraining grand coordinators.
translations.idiomatic: He first memorialized on five themes: cultivating the sovereign's virtue, drawing close to ministers, enforcing the law, honoring Confucian conduct, and restraining provincial overseers.

sentences.zh: 尋劾罷禮部尚書徐學謨、南京戶部尚書張士佩。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached and removed Minister of Rites Xu Xuemo and Nanjing Minister of Revenue Zhang Shipei.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached and brought about the dismissal of Minister of Rites Xu Xuemo and Nanjing Minister of Revenue Zhang Shipei.

sentences.zh: 徐學謨者，嘉定縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Xuemo was a man of Jiading county.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuemo came from Jiading county.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，為荊州知府。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he was prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing he served as prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 景恭王之藩德安，欲奪荊州城北沙市地。

translations.literal: When Prince Gong of Jing took up his fief at De'an, he wished to seize the land of Shashi north of Jingzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Gong of Jing was enfeoffed at De'an, he sought to seize Shashi market north of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 學謨力抗不予，為王所劾，下撫按逮問，改官。

translations.literal: Xuemo strenuously resisted and would not grant it; the prince impeached him, and he was sent down to the grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner for interrogation and was transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo resisted firmly and refused; the prince impeached him, and he was sent down to the provincial authorities for questioning and transferred.

sentences.zh: 荊州人德之，稱沙市為「徐市」。

translations.literal: The people of Jingzhou honored him and called Shashi "Xu Market."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jingzhou honored him and called Shashi "Xu's Market."

sentences.zh: 居正素與厚。

translations.literal: Juzheng had long been on close terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng had long been intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，累遷右副都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he rose successively to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli he rose to vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 居正歸葬父，學謨事之謹，召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Juzheng returned to bury his father, Xuemo served him with care and was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng returned to bury his father, Xuemo attended him devotedly and was summoned as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 越二年，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Two years later he was promoted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 自弘治後，禮部長非翰林不授，惟席書以言「大禮」故，由他曹遷；

translations.literal: Since Hongzhi, the head of the Ministry of Rites had not been appointed except from the Hanlin Academy; only Xi Shu, because of the "Great Rites" controversy, was transferred from another bureau;
translations.idiomatic: Since Hongzhi, ministers of rites had been drawn from the Hanlin Academy; only Xi Shu, because of the Great Rites controversy, had come from another bureau;

sentences.zh: 萬士和不由翰林，然先歷其部侍郎。

translations.literal: Wan Shihe was not from the Hanlin, yet he had first served as vice minister in that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shihe had not been a Hanlin scholar, but he had first served as vice minister in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 學謨徑拜尚書，廷臣以居正故，莫敢言。

translations.literal: Xuemo was appointed minister directly; court officials, because of Juzheng, did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo was appointed minister outright; because of Juzheng, no one at court dared object.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，學謨急締姻於大學士申時行以自固。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, Xuemo hastily arranged a marriage alliance with Grand Secretary Shen Shixing to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death Xuemo hurried to ally himself by marriage with Grand Secretary Shen Shixing.

sentences.zh: 及奉命擇壽宮，通政參議梁子琦劾其始結居正，繼附時行，詔為奪子琦俸。

translations.literal: When ordered to select the imperial tomb site, Vice Commissioner of the Court for the Imperial Clan Liang Ziqi impeached him for first attaching to Juzheng and then to Shixing; an edict stripped Ziqi of one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ordered to choose the imperial tomb site, vice commissioner Liang Ziqi impeached him for clinging first to Juzheng and then to Shixing; the throne fined Ziqi a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 元標復劾之，遂令致仕歸。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao impeached him again, and he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao impeached him again, and he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 慈寧宮災，元標復上時政六事，中言：「臣曩進無欲之訓，陛下試自省，果無欲耶？

translations.literal: When the Cining Palace burned, Yuanbiao again memorialized on six current affairs, saying among other things: "Your servant once advanced the teaching of freedom from desire; let Your Majesty examine yourself—are you truly without desire?
translations.idiomatic: When the Cining Palace burned, Yuanbiao memorialized again on six affairs of state, writing among other things: "I once urged the teaching of freedom from desire. Let Your Majesty examine yourself: are you truly without desire?

sentences.zh: 寡欲耶？

translations.literal: Or with few desires?
translations.idiomatic: Or only with few desires?

sentences.zh: 語云：『欲人勿聞，莫若勿為。

translations.literal: The saying runs: 'If you do not wish others to hear, better not to do it.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'If you do not wish others to hear, better not to do it.'

sentences.zh: 』陛下誠宜翻然自省，加意培養。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should indeed turn and examine yourself and give added care to cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should turn inward, examine yourself, and devote yourself to self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」當是時，帝方壯齡，留意聲色遊宴，謂元標刺己，怒甚，降旨譙責。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was in his vigorous years and devoted to music, women, and feasting; he thought Yuanbiao was satirizing him and was very angry, issuing an edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then in his prime and devoted to pleasure; he took Yuanbiao's words as a personal attack, grew furious, and issued a rebuke.

sentences.zh: 首輔時行以元標己門生，而劾罷其姻學謨，亦心憾，遂謫南京刑部照磨。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Shixing, because Yuanbiao was his own student yet had impeached his son-in-law Xuemo, also resented him and had him demoted to Registrar in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Shen Shixing, whose student Yuanbiao had been, resented him for impeaching his son-in-law Xuemo and had him demoted to registrar in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 就遷兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was soon made Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 召改吏部，進員外郎，以病免。

translations.literal: Recalled to the Ministry of Personnel, he was promoted Vice Director and then resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to the Ministry of Personnel, he was promoted vice director and then resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 起補驗封。

translations.literal: Recalled again, he was appointed to Seals and Investitures.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned again, he was appointed to the bureau of seals and investitures.

sentences.zh: 陳吏治十事，民瘼八事，疏幾萬言。

translations.literal: He set forth ten matters on official administration and eight on the people's suffering, the memorial running to nearly ten thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out ten proposals on official administration and eight on popular distress in a memorial of nearly ten thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 文選缺員外郎，尚書宋糸熏請用元標，久不獲命，糸熏連疏趣之。

translations.literal: When the vice directorship in Appointments fell vacant, Minister Song Xu requested Yuanbiao's appointment; long without approval, Song sent successive memorials urging it.
translations.idiomatic: When a vice directorship in appointments fell vacant, Minister Song Xu recommended Yuanbiao; the appointment was long delayed, and Song sent repeated memorials urging it.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊文煥、御史何選亦以為言。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yang Wenhuan and Censor He Xuan also spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yang Wenhuan and censor He Xuan spoke up for him as well.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詰責糸熏，謫文煥、選於外，而調元標南京。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, rebuked Song Xu, and banished Wenhuan and Xuan abroad while transferring Yuanbiao to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, rebuked Song Xu, banished Wenhuan and Xuan from the capital, and transferred Yuanbiao to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書石星論救，亦被譙讓。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Shi Xing pleaded in his defense and was also rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Shi Xing spoke in his defense and was rebuked as well.

sentences.zh: 元標居南京三年，移疾歸。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao lived in Nanjing three years and then resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao spent three years in Nanjing, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，起本部郎中，不赴。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Director in the ministry but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was appointed director in the ministry but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 旋遭母憂，裏居講學，從遊者日眾，名高天下。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered his mother's mourning; living at home he lectured on learning, and daily followers grew; his fame rose throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his mother; at home he taught, his following grew daily, and his fame spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 中外疏薦遺佚，凡數十百上，莫不以元標為首。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court, memorials recommending overlooked men numbered in the tens and hundreds, and all placed Yuanbiao first.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from within and beyond the court recommending overlooked talent numbered in the hundreds, and nearly all named Yuanbiao first.

sentences.zh: 卒不用。

translations.literal: In the end he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was not recalled.

sentences.zh: 家食垂三十年。

translations.literal: He lived at home in retirement for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement at home for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，召拜大理卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was summoned as Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, he was summoned as chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 未至，進刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was advanced Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he was promoted vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年四月還朝，首進和衷之說，言：「今日國事，皆二十年諸臣醞釀所成。

translations.literal: Returning to court in the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi, he first advanced the doctrine of harmonious purpose, saying: "Today's affairs of state are all the product of twenty years of ferment among the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court in the fourth month of Tianqi 1 and first advanced the doctrine of harmony, writing: "Today's affairs are the fruit of twenty years' ferment among court officials.

sentences.zh: 往者不以進賢讓能為事，日錮賢逐能，而言事者又不降心平氣，專務分門立戶。

translations.literal: Formerly men did not make advancing the worthy and yielding place to the able their business, but daily imprisoned the worthy and drove out the able; while those who spoke on affairs would not lower their hearts and calm their tempers, but devoted themselves to forming factions and raising cliques.
translations.idiomatic: They ceased to advance the worthy and yield to the able, instead shutting up talent and driving out ability; and those who spoke on policy would not lower their voices or calm their tempers, but devoted themselves to forming factions.

sentences.zh: 臣謂今日急務，惟朝臣和衷而已。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that today's urgent task is only that court ministers harmonize their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that today's urgent task is for ministers to harmonize their purpose.

sentences.zh: 朝臣和，天地之和自應。

translations.literal: When court ministers are harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds of itself.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers are at one, the harmony of heaven and earth responds in turn.

sentences.zh: 向之論人論事者，各懷偏見，偏生迷，迷生執，執而為我，不復知有人，禍且移於國。

translations.literal: Those who formerly judged men and affairs each harbored bias; bias breeds delusion, delusion breeds obstinacy, and obstinacy becomes self—no longer knowing that others exist—and calamity shifts to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Those who judge men and affairs each carry bias; bias breeds delusion, delusion breeds obstinacy, and obstinacy becomes self-interest until one no longer sees others—and calamity falls on the state.

sentences.zh: 今與諸臣約，論一人當惟公惟平，毋輕搖筆端，論一事當懲前慮後，毋輕試耳食，以天下萬世之心，衡天下萬世之人與事，則議論公，而國家自享安靜和平之福。

translations.literal: Now I covenant with all ministers: in judging a man, be fair and even and do not lightly move the brush; in judging an affair, take warning from the past and look to the future and do not lightly trust hearsay. With the mind of all ages and ten thousand generations, weigh the men and affairs of all ages and ten thousand generations—then discussion will be public and the state will enjoy the blessing of quiet peace.
translations.idiomatic: I ask all ministers: in judging a man, be fair and do not lightly strike with the pen; in judging a matter, learn from the past and look to the future and do not trust rumor. Weigh men and affairs with the mind of the ages, and debate will be public and the realm will know quiet peace.

sentences.zh: 」因薦塗宗浚、李邦華等十八人。

translations.literal: " He thereupon recommended Tu Zongjun, Li Banghua, and eighteen others.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Tu Zongjun, Li Banghua, and eighteen others.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒納。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict of praise and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 居二日，復陳拔茅闡幽、理財振武數事，及保泰四規。

translations.literal: Two days later he again set forth pulling up grass to reveal the hidden, managing finances, and reviving martial affairs, and the four rules for preserving stability.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he memorialized again on uncovering hidden talent, managing finances, reviving military strength, and the four rules for preserving stability.

sentences.zh: 且請召用葉茂才、趙南星、高攀龍、劉宗周、丁元薦，而恤錄羅大纮、雒於仁等十五人。

translations.literal: He also asked that Ye Maocai, Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Liu Zongzhou, and Ding Yuanjian be summoned, and that Luo Daxuan, Luo Yuren, and fifteen others be granted posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Ye Maocai, Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Liu Zongzhou, and Ding Yuanjian be recalled, and that Luo Daxuan, Luo Yuren, and fifteen others receive posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 帝亦褒納。

translations.literal: The emperor again praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again responded with praise.

sentences.zh: 初，元標立朝，以方嚴見憚，晚節務為和易。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuanbiao stood at court, he was feared for his stern rectitude; in his later years he strove to be easy and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanbiao first entered office he was feared for his stern rectitude; in later years he sought ease and harmony.

sentences.zh: 或議其遜初仕時，元標笑曰：「大臣與言官異。

translations.literal: Some criticized him for falling short of his early career; Yuanbiao smiled and said, "A great minister differs from a remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he had grown milder than in his youth; Yuanbiao smiled and said, "A senior minister is not a remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 風裁踔絕，言官事也。

translations.literal: Bold and transcendent bearing is the business of remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Daring, uncompromising speech is the remonstrator's role.

sentences.zh: 大臣非大利害，即當護持國體，可如少年悻動耶？

translations.literal: Unless the harm or benefit to the state is great, a great minister ought to uphold the dignity of the polity—can he act like a hotheaded youth?
translations.idiomatic: Unless the state's interest is gravely at stake, a senior minister must uphold the body's dignity—can he behave like an impetuous youth?

sentences.zh: 」時朋黨方盛，元標心惡之，思矯其弊，故其所薦引不專一途。

translations.literal: At that time factionalism was in full flood; Yuanbiao detested it and wished to correct the abuse, and therefore those he recommended were not all of one path.
translations.idiomatic: Factionalism was then at its height; Yuanbiao hated it and sought to correct the abuse, so his recommendations did not follow a single factional line.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲舉用李三才，因言路不與，元標即中止。

translations.literal: He once wished to employ Li Sancai, but because the remonstrance circuit would not agree, Yuanbiao at once desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He once wished to appoint Li Sancai, but when the remonstrance offices objected, he dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 王德完譏其首鼠，元標亦不較。

translations.literal: Wang Dewan mocked him as indecisive; Yuanbiao did not contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dewan mocked him as timid and wavering; Yuanbiao did not answer him.

sentences.zh: 南京御史王允成等以兩人不和，請帝諭解。

translations.literal: Nanjing Censor Wang Yuncheng and others, because the two men were not on good terms, asked the emperor to instruct a reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing censor Wang Yuncheng and others, noting discord between the two men, asked the emperor to urge a reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 元標言：「臣與德完初無纖芥，此必有人交構其間。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao said: "Your servant and Dewan had no shred of difference at first; someone must be sowing discord between us.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao replied: "Dewan and I were never at odds; someone must be playing us against each other.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗語朝士曰：『方今上在沖歲，敵在門庭，只有同心共濟。

translations.literal: Your servant once told court gentlemen: 'Today the sovereign is still young, the enemy is at the gate—we must only join hearts and cross together.
translations.idiomatic: I once told colleagues: 'The sovereign is still a child and the enemy stands at the gate; we must stand together.

sentences.zh: 倘復黨同伐異，在國則不忠，在家則不孝。

translations.literal: If again we form factions to attack those unlike us, in the state it is disloyalty, in the family it is unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: If we again form factions and attack one another, that is disloyalty to the state and unfilial to the family.

sentences.zh: 世自有無偏無黨之路，奈何從室內起戈矛耶？

translations.literal: The world has its own path of impartiality and freedom from factions—why raise spears within the house?'
translations.idiomatic: There is a path without bias or faction—why draw swords under our own roof?'

sentences.zh: 』」帝嗣位已久，而先朝廢死諸臣猶未贈恤，元標再陳闡幽之典，言益懇切。

translations.literal: The emperor had long succeeded, yet the dismissed and dead ministers of the previous reign were still not granted posthumous honors; Yuanbiao again set forth the canon for revealing the hidden, his words all the more earnest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long been on the throne, yet ministers disgraced and killed under the previous reign still lacked posthumous honors; Yuanbiao memorialized again, his words growing more urgent.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月改吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he was made Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year he was made left vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 未到官，拜左都御史。

translations.literal: Before he took office he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up that post he was appointed left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，典外察，去留惟公。

translations.literal: The next year he conducted the outer review; who stayed and who left depended solely on fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he conducted the outer review of officials, retaining or dismissing solely on merit.

sentences.zh: 御史潘汝楨、過庭訓雅有物議，及庭訓秩滿，汝楨註考溢美。

translations.literal: Censors Pan Ruzhen and Guo Tingxun had long been objects of public criticism; when Tingxun's term expired, Ruzhen entered an evaluation overflowing with praise.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Pan Ruzhen and Guo Tingxun were widely criticized; when Tingxun's term ended, Ruzhen entered a glowing evaluation for him.

sentences.zh: 元標疏論之，兩人並引疾去。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao memorialized against this, and both men resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao attacked the report in a memorial, and both men resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 已，言丁已京察不公，專禁錮異己，請收錄章家禎、丁元薦、史記事、沈正宗等二十二人。

translations.literal: Later he said the dingsi capital review was unfair, that it chiefly imprisoned those unlike the faction, and asked that Zhang Jiazhen, Ding Yuanjian, Shi Jishi, Shen Zhengzong, and twenty-two others be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He then charged that the dingsi capital review had been unfair, chiefly used to shut up dissenters, and asked that Zhang Jiazhen, Ding Yuanjian, Shi Jishi, Shen Zhengzong, and twenty-two others be restored.

sentences.zh: 由是諸臣多獲昭雪。

translations.literal: Thereupon many ministers were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials were thereby rehabilitated.

sentences.zh: 又言：「明詔收召遺佚，而諸老臣所處猶是三十年前應得之官，宜添註三品崇秩，昭陛下褒尊耆舊至意。

translations.literal: He also said: "The bright edict calls back the overlooked, yet the old ministers are still given only the offices they deserved thirty years ago; additional third-rank honorary posts should be added to show Your Majesty's intent to honor the aged."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote that the edict recalling overlooked men still left veteran ministers with only the ranks they had earned decades before, and urged added third-rank honors to show the throne's respect for age.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 於是兩京太常、太仆、光祿三卿各增二員。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three ministers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of the Imperial Stud, and the Court of the Imperial Banquets in both capitals each gained two additional posts.
translations.idiomatic: The three courts of sacrifices, the imperial stud, and imperial banquets in both capitals each gained two additional posts.

sentences.zh: 孫慎行之論「紅丸」也，元標亦上疏曰：「乾坤所以不毀者，惟此綱常；

translations.literal: When Sun Shenxing argued the "red pill" affair, Yuanbiao also memorialized: "Heaven and Earth are not destroyed because of this bond of right conduct;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Shenxing took up the "red pill" affair, Yuanbiao memorialized as well: "Heaven and earth endure because of the bonds of right conduct;

sentences.zh: 綱常所以植立者，恃此信史。

translations.literal: and this bond is established by relying on this faithful history.
translations.idiomatic: and those bonds stand only because faithful history preserves them.

sentences.zh: 臣去年舟過南中，南中士大夫爭言先帝猝然而崩，大事未明，難以傳信。

translations.literal: Your servant last year passed through the south by boat; southern gentlemen all said the late emperor died suddenly and the great matter is unclear, hard to pass on in faithful record.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, passing through the south, I heard everywhere that the late emperor died suddenly, that the great matter remains unclear, and that truth cannot yet be written.

sentences.zh: 臣初不謂然。

translations.literal: Your servant at first did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: At first I did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 及既入都，為人言先帝盛德，宜速登信史。

translations.literal: Once in the capital, speaking of the late emperor's abundant virtue, one should quickly enter it in faithful history.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital I spoke of entering the late emperor's virtues in the veritable record.

sentences.zh: 諸臣曰：『言及先帝彌留大事，令人閣筆，誰敢領此？

translations.literal: The gentlemen said: 'Speaking of the late emperor's final illness and the great matter makes one lay down the brush—who dares undertake this?'
translations.idiomatic: They answered: 'To speak of the late emperor's final illness is to lay down the brush—who dares write it?'

sentences.zh: 』臣始有疑於前日之言。

translations.literal: Your servant then had doubts about what was said on the earlier day.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did I credit what I had heard in the south.

sentences.zh: 元輔方從哲不伸討賊之義，反行賞奸之典，即謂無其心，何以自解於世？

translations.literal: Chief Minister Fang Congzhe did not extend the duty of punishing the villain, but instead carried out the canon of rewarding the wicked—even if one says he had no such heart, how can he explain himself to the world?
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Fang Congzhe did not pursue the assassins but rewarded the guilty; even if he lacked murderous intent, how can he answer the world?

sentences.zh: 且從哲秉政七年，未聞建樹何事，但聞馬上一日三趣戰，喪我十萬師徒。

translations.literal: Moreover, Congzhe held power seven years without a single achievement heard of, but only heard of urging battle three times in one day on horseback, losing one hundred thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years in power he built nothing, yet urged battle three times in a single day from horseback and lost a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 訊問誰秉國成，而使先帝震驚，奸人闖宮，豺狼當路，憸邪亂政？

translations.literal: Ask who held the reins of state and allowed the late emperor to be shaken, villains to burst into the palace, wolves to block the road, and slanderers to disorder government?
translations.idiomatic: Who held the reins when the late emperor was shaken, villains burst into the palace, wolves blocked the road, and slanderers ran the government?

sentences.zh: 從哲何詞以對？

translations.literal: With what words can Congzhe answer?
translations.idiomatic: What answer can Congzhe give?

sentences.zh: 從來懲戒亂賊，全在信史。

translations.literal: Punishing rebellious villains has always depended on faithful history.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment of traitors has always rested on the faithful record.

sentences.zh: 失今不成，安所底止。

translations.literal: If it is not done now, where will it end?
translations.idiomatic: Fail to write it now, and where will justice end?

sentences.zh: 」時刑部尚書黃克纘希內廷意，群小和之，而從哲世居京師，黨附者眾，崔文升黨復彌縫於內，格慎行與眾議，皆不得伸。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Justice Huang Kexuan curried favor with the inner court, petty men echoed him, and Congzhe had long lived in the capital with many partisans; Cui Wensheng's faction further smoothed matters within, blocking Shenxing and public opinion so that none could prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Huang Kexuan courted the inner palace; petty men echoed him; Congzhe's capital faction was large; Cui Wensheng's party smoothed matters inside—so Shenxing and public opinion could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 未幾，慎行及王紀偕逐，元標疏救，不聽。

translations.literal: Before long Shenxing and Wang Ji were driven out together; Yuanbiao memorialized in their defense but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shenxing and Wang Ji were expelled together; Yuanbiao pleaded for them in vain.

sentences.zh: 元標自還朝以來，不為危言激論，與物無猜。

translations.literal: Since Yuanbiao returned to court he had not spoken harsh or provocative words and bore no suspicion toward others.
translations.idiomatic: Since his return Yuanbiao had avoided harsh rhetoric and bore no grudges.

sentences.zh: 然小人以其東林也，猶忌之。

translations.literal: Yet petty men, because he was of the Donglin faction, still envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty men still resented him as a Donglin man.

sentences.zh: 給事中朱童蒙、郭允厚、郭興治慮明年京察不利己，潛謀驅逐。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Zhu Tongmeng, Guo Yunhou, and Guo Xingzhi, fearing the next capital review would go against them, secretly plotted expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Zhu Tongmeng, Guo Yunhou, and Guo Xingzhi, fearing the coming capital review, plotted secretly to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 會元標與馮從吾建首善書院，集同誌講學，童蒙首請禁之。

translations.literal: When Yuanbiao and Feng Congwu founded the Shou Shan Academy to gather like-minded men for lecturing, Tongmeng first asked that it be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanbiao and Feng Congwu founded the Shou Shan Academy for joint study, Tongmeng was first to demand its closure.

sentences.zh: 元標疏辨求去，帝已慰留，允厚復疏劾，語尤妄誕。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao memorialized in defense and asked to leave; the emperor had already comforted him and retained him, but Yunhou memorialized again in impeachment with words especially wild and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao defended himself and asked to withdraw; the emperor had already urged him to stay, but Yunhou impeached him again with wild charges.

sentences.zh: 而魏忠賢方竊柄，傳旨謂宋室之亡由於講學，將加嚴譴。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian was then usurping power; a transmitted edict said the Song dynasty's fall came from lecturing, and severe punishment would follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian, seizing power, transmitted word that the Song fell through lecturing and threatened severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 葉向高力辨，且乞同去，乃得溫旨。

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao argued forcefully and asked to leave with him; only then came a mild edict.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao argued fiercely and offered to resign with him; only then came a mild edict.

sentences.zh: 興治及允厚復交章力攻，興治至比之山東妖賊。

translations.literal: Xingzhi and Yunhou again submitted successive memorials attacking fiercely; Xingzhi even compared him to the sorcerers of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi and Yunhou attacked again; Xingzhi even compared him to Shandong sorcerers.

sentences.zh: 元標連疏請益力，詔加太子少保，乘傳歸。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao memorialized to leave all the more strenuously; an edict added him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and sent him home by fast courier.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao begged to leave with growing force; the throne made him grand guardian of the heir apparent and sent him home by express.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上《老臣去國情深疏》，歷陳軍國大計，而以寡欲進規，人為傳誦。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he submitted the memorial "An Old Minister Leaving Court with Deep Feeling," setting forth military and state plans at length and admonishing with few desires; men copied and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell he submitted "An Old Minister's Deep Feeling on Leaving Court," laying out state and military policy and urging restraint of desire; men copied and recited it.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史張訥請毀天下講壇，力詆元標，忠賢遂矯旨削奪。

translations.literal: The next year Censor Zhang Na asked that lecture platforms throughout the realm be destroyed and vehemently denounced Yuanbiao; Zhongxian forged an edict stripping his honors.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhang Na demanded the destruction of lecture halls empire-wide and attacked Yuanbiao; Zhongxian forged an edict stripping his honors.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太子太保、吏部尚書，謚忠介。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent and minister of personnel, with the posthumous name Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 童蒙等既劾元標，遂得罪清議，尋以年例外遷。

translations.literal: After Tongmeng and the others impeached Yuanbiao, they offended public opinion and soon were transferred out on account of years of service.
translations.idiomatic: After impeaching Yuanbiao, Tongmeng and his allies offended public opinion and were soon transferred on seniority.

sentences.zh: 及忠賢得誌，三人並召還。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian had his way, all three were recalled.
