translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian triumphed, all three were recalled.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，允厚至戶部尚書、太子太保。

translations.literal: Within a year Yunhou reached Minister of Revenue and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Yunhou rose to minister of revenue and grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 童蒙至右副都御史，巡撫延綏，母死不持服，為忠賢建生祠。

translations.literal: Tongmeng reached Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yan-sui; he did not observe mourning for his mother's death and built a living shrine for Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Tongmeng became vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yan-sui; he failed to mourn his mother and built a living shrine to Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 興治亦加至太仆卿。

translations.literal: Xingzhi was also raised to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi rose to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，三人並麗逆案雲。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, all three were listed in the case of traitors.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian fell, all three were named in the roll of traitors.

sentences.zh: 孫慎行，字聞斯，武進人。

translations.literal: Sun Shenxing, styled Wensi, was a man of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shenxing, whose style name was Wensi, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 幼習聞外祖唐順之緒論，即嗜學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the inherited doctrines of his maternal grandfather Tang Shunzhi and at once loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he absorbed the teachings of his maternal grandfather Tang Shunzhi and took to learning at once.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年舉進士第三人，授編修，累官左庶子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he placed third among jinshi and was appointed Compiler; he rose successively to Left Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 23 he placed third on the jinshi list, was appointed compiler, and rose to left sub-reader.

sentences.zh: 數請假裏居，鍵戶息交，覃精理學。

translations.literal: Several times he asked leave to live at home, bolted his door and cut off social ties, and delved deeply into Neo-Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sought leave to live at home, shut his door to visitors, and pursued Neo-Confucian learning in depth.

sentences.zh: 當事請見，率不納。

translations.literal: When those in power asked to see him, he generally did not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Men in power who sought audience were usually turned away.

sentences.zh: 有以政事詢者，不答。

translations.literal: When asked about affairs of government, he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Questions about government he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 四十一年五月，由少詹事擢禮部右侍郎，署部事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the forty-first year he was promoted from Vice Director of the Hanlin Academy to Vice Minister of Rites and directed ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 41 he was promoted from vice director of the Hanlin Academy to vice minister of rites, directing the ministry.

sentences.zh: 當是時，郊廟大享諸禮，帝二十余年不躬親，東宮輟講至八年，皇長孫九齡未就外傅，瑞王二十三未婚，楚宗人久錮未釋，代王廢長立幼，久不更正，臣僚章奏一切留中，福府莊田取盈四萬頃，慎行並切諫。

translations.literal: At that time, for more than twenty years the emperor had not personally attended the great suburban sacrifices and temple offerings; lectures for the heir apparent had ceased for eight years; the eldest imperial grandson, nine sui, had not yet been given an outer tutor; the Prince of Rui, twenty-three, was still unmarried; men of the Chu princely house had long been imprisoned without release; the Prince of Dai had deposed the eldest and established the younger, long uncorrected; memorials from ministers were all held back; and the Prince of Fu's estate lands had been taken to the full forty thousand qing—Shenxing remonstrated sharply on all these.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years the emperor had not performed the great sacrifices; the heir apparent's lectures had ceased for eight years; the eldest imperial grandson of nine sui had no outer tutor; the Prince of Rui at twenty-three remained unmarried; Chu clansmen languished in prison; the Prince of Dai had set aside the eldest for the younger without correction; memorials were held back; and the Prince of Fu's estate had swollen to forty thousand qing—Shenxing remonstrated on every point.

sentences.zh: 已，念東宮開講，皇孫出閣，系宗社安危，疏至七八上。

translations.literal: Later, mindful that lectures for the heir apparent and the imperial grandson's emergence from the palace bore on the altars of state, he memorialized seven or eight times.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing that the heir apparent's lectures and the imperial grandson's schooling touched the fate of the dynasty, he memorialized seven or eight times.

sentences.zh: 代王廢長子鼎渭，立愛子鼎莎，李廷機為侍郎時主之，其後，群臣爭者百余疏，帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai had deposed the eldest son Dingwei and established the beloved son Dingsha; when Li Tingji was vice minister he had supported this, and afterward more than a hundred memorials from ministers contended, yet the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai had deposed his eldest son Dingwei for the favored Dingsha; Vice Minister Li Tingji had backed the change, and though more than a hundred memorials followed, the emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 慎行屢疏爭，乃獲更置。

translations.literal: Shenxing memorialized repeatedly in contention and at last secured a reversal.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing protested repeatedly until the succession was corrected.

sentences.zh: 楚宗人擊殺巡撫趙可懷，為首六人論死，復錮英憔等二十三人於高墻，禁蘊鈁等二十三人於遠地。

translations.literal: Men of the Chu princely house had killed Grand Coordinator Zhao Kehuai; six ringleaders were sentenced to death, yet Yingqiao and twenty-two others were again imprisoned in the high wall and Yun'ang and twenty-three others confined in distant places.
translations.idiomatic: Chu clansmen had killed grand coordinator Zhao Kehuai; six ringleaders were sentenced to death, yet Yingqiao and twenty-two others were walled up again and Yun'ang and twenty-three others sent to distant confinement.

sentences.zh: 慎行力白其非叛，諸人由此獲釋。

translations.literal: Shenxing strenuously argued they were not rebels, and the men were thereby released.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing insisted they were not rebels, and the men were released.

sentences.zh: 皇太子儲位雖定，福王尚留京師，須莊田四萬頃乃行，宵小多窺伺。

translations.literal: Though the crown prince's place was settled, the Prince of Fu still remained in the capital and would not depart until estate lands of forty thousand qing were granted; petty men watched for chances.
translations.idiomatic: Though the crown prince's place was fixed, the Prince of Fu lingered in the capital until granted forty thousand qing; opportunists watched and waited.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請之國者愈眾，帝愈遲之。

translations.literal: Court ministers who asked that he go to his fief grew ever more numerous, yet the emperor delayed ever more.
translations.idiomatic: More courtiers urged him to his fief, yet the emperor delayed ever longer.

sentences.zh: 慎行疏十余上，不見省。

translations.literal: Shenxing memorialized more than ten times without response.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing memorialized more than ten times without answer.

sentences.zh: 最後，貴妃復請帝留王慶太后七旬壽節，群議益籍籍。

translations.literal: At last the honored consort again asked the emperor to keep the prince for the seventieth birthday of the Dowager of Qing, and public talk grew clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: At last the honored consort asked the emperor to keep the prince for the dowager of Qing's seventieth birthday, and public uproar grew.

sentences.zh: 慎行乃合文武諸臣伏闕力請，大學士葉向高亦爭之強。

translations.literal: Shenxing then joined civil and military ministers in kneeling at the palace gate to press the request; Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao also argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing then joined civil and military officials in kneeling at the palace gate; Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao argued fiercely as well.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，許明年季春之國，群情始安。

translations.literal: The emperor, having no choice, promised he would go to his fief in the coming spring, and public feeling was then calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, cornered, promised departure the following spring, and public feeling eased.

sentences.zh: 韓敬科場之議，慎行擬黜敬。

translations.literal: In the Han Jing examination scandal, Shenxing proposed demoting Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the examination scandal involving Han Jing, Shenxing proposed demoting Jing.

sentences.zh: 而家居時素講學東林，敬黨尤忌之。

translations.literal: Yet while living at home he had long lectured with the Donglin faction, and Jing's faction especially hated him.
translations.idiomatic: At home he had long associated with the Donglin movement, and Jing's faction hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 會吏部缺侍郎，廷議改右侍郎李鋕於左，而以慎行為右，命俱未下。

translations.literal: When a vice ministership in Personnel fell vacant, court opinion moved Right Vice Minister Li Zhi to the left and Shenxing to the right; the orders had not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: When a personnel vice ministership fell vacant, court opinion moved Li Zhi from the right to the left and Shenxing to the right; the orders had not yet been issued.

sentences.zh: 御史過廷訓因言鋕未履任，何復推慎行，給事中亓詩教和之。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Tingxun thereupon said Li Zhi had not yet taken office—why promote Shenxing? Supervising Secretary Qi Shijiao echoed him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Tingxun objected that Li Zhi had not yet taken office—why advance Shenxing? Supervising secretary Qi Shijiao agreed.

sentences.zh: 慎行遂四疏乞歸，出城候命，帝乃許之。

translations.literal: Shenxing thereupon submitted four memorials asking to return home, went outside the city to await the edict, and the emperor then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing submitted four memorials asking to retire, waited outside the city for the edict, and the emperor let him go.

sentences.zh: 已而京察，御史韓浚等以趣福王之國，謂慎行邀功，列之拾遺疏中。

translations.literal: In the capital review, Censor Han Jun and others, because he had pressed the Prince of Fu's departure, said Shenxing was courting merit and listed him in the memorial on overlooked remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital review, censor Han Jun and others, citing his pressure on the Prince of Fu, called him a glory-seeker and listed him among remonstrance officials to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝察其無罪，獲免。

translations.literal: The emperor saw he was without guilt and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw he was innocent and spared him.

sentences.zh: 熹宗立，召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended, he was summoned as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong took the throne, he was summoned as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 初，光宗大漸，鴻臚寺丞李可灼以紅鉛丸藥進。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Guangzong was gravely ill, Court of State Ceremonial Director Li Kezhuo presented medicine of red lead pills.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong lay gravely ill, Court of State Ceremonial director Li Kezhuo presented red-lead pills.

sentences.zh: 俄帝崩，廷臣交章劾之。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died, and court ministers submitted successive memorials impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon died, and courtiers impeached him in succession.

sentences.zh: 大學士方從哲擬旨令引疾歸，賚以金幣。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe drafted an edict ordering him to retire citing illness and bestowed gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe drafted an edict ordering Kezhuo to retire citing illness and bestowed gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年四月，慎行還朝，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi, Shenxing returned to court and memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianqi 1, Shenxing returned to court and memorialized:

sentences.zh: 先帝驟崩，雖雲夙疾，實緣醫人用藥不審。

translations.literal: The late emperor died suddenly; though it is said to have been a long-standing illness, in truth it came from the physician's careless use of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor died suddenly; though called a long illness, it came from careless medicine.

sentences.zh: 閱邸報，知李可灼紅丸乃首輔方從哲所進。

translations.literal: Reading the court gazette, I know Li Kezhuo's red pills were presented by Chief Minister Fang Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: The gazette shows that Li Kezhuo's red pills were presented by Chief Minister Fang Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 夫可灼官非太醫，紅丸不知何藥，乃敢突然以進。

translations.literal: Kezhuo's office is not that of the Imperial Medical Academy, and what the red pills were is unknown—yet he dared suddenly to present them.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhuo was no imperial physician, and no one knows what the red pills were—yet he dared present them.

sentences.zh: 昔許悼公飲世子藥而卒，世子即自殺，《春秋》猶書之為弒。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xu of Zheng's son made him drink medicine and he died; the son then killed himself, yet the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 still records it as regicide.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xu of Zheng's heir gave him medicine and he died, the heir killed himself, yet the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 still records regicide.

sentences.zh: 然則從哲宜何居？

translations.literal: Then with what status should Congzhe stand?
translations.idiomatic: What standing does Congzhe deserve?

sentences.zh: 速引劍自裁以謝先帝，義之上也；

translations.literal: Swiftly to draw his sword and take his own life to apologize to the late emperor is the highest righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: The highest righteousness would be to draw his sword and die apologizing to the late emperor;

sentences.zh: 合門席稿以待司寇，義之次也；

translations.literal: to sit on straw at his gate awaiting the Minister of Justice is the next;
translations.idiomatic: the next, to sit on straw awaiting the minister of justice;

sentences.zh: 乃悍然不顧，至舉朝共攻可灼，僅令回籍調理，豈不以己實薦之，恐與同罪與？

translations.literal: yet he defiantly paid no heed, and when the whole court together attacked Kezhuo, he was only ordered to return home and recuperate—is it not because he had in fact recommended him and feared sharing the crime?
translations.idiomatic: yet he defied all decency, and when the court attacked Kezhuo, allowed him merely to return home—fearing shared guilt because he had recommended him?

sentences.zh: 臣以為從哲縱無弒之心，卻有弒之事；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Congzhe, though without a heart of regicide, had the deed of regicide;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Congzhe, though he may lack a murderer's heart, committed a murderer's act;

sentences.zh: 欲辭弒之名，難免弒之實。

translations.literal: wishing to escape the name of regicide, he cannot escape the reality of regicide.
translations.idiomatic: to escape the name of regicide, he cannot escape its reality.

sentences.zh: 實錄中即欲為君父諱，不敢不直書方從哲連進藥二丸，須臾帝崩，恐百口無能為天下後世解也。

translations.literal: In the veritable record, even if one wishes to spare the ruler and father, one dare not but write plainly that Fang Congzhe presented two pills in succession and the emperor died in a moment—lest a hundred mouths be unable to explain it to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: In the veritable record, even to spare the late emperor one must write plainly that Fang Congzhe presented two pills in succession and the emperor died at once—or a hundred mouths cannot explain it to posterity.

sentences.zh: 然從哲之罪實不止此。

translations.literal: Yet Congzhe's crime does not stop there.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe's crimes do not end there.

sentences.zh: 先是則有皇貴妃欲為皇后事，古未有天子既崩而立後者。

translations.literal: Before this was the affair of the honored consort wishing to become empress; in antiquity there was never making a consort after the Son of Heaven had died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier came the honored consort's bid to become empress—unprecedented after a sovereign's death.

sentences.zh: 倘非禮官執奏，言路力持，幾何不遺禍宗社哉！

translations.literal: Had not the ritual officials memorialized in opposition and the remonstrance circuit held firm, how would calamity not have been left to the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Had ritual officials and remonstrators not held firm, what calamity might not have befallen the dynasty!

sentences.zh: 繼此則有謚皇祖為恭皇帝事。

translations.literal: Following this was the affair of posthumously honoring the imperial grandfather as Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Next came posthumously honoring the imperial grandfather as Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 歷考晉、隋、周、宋，其末世亡國之君率謚曰「恭」，而以加之我皇祖，豈真不學無術？

translations.literal: Examining Jin, Sui, Zhou, and Song, their last rulers who lost states are mostly posthumously styled "Gong"; to apply this to our imperial grandfather—is it truly ignorance?
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Sui, Zhou, and Song, doomed last rulers were often styled "Gong"; to give our grandfather that style—was it mere ignorance?

sentences.zh: 實乃咒詛君國，等於亡王，其設心謂何？

translations.literal: In truth it curses the ruler and state, equaling a perished king—what was the intent?
translations.idiomatic: It cursed ruler and state like a doomed king—what was the intent?

sentences.zh: 後此則有選侍垂簾聽政事。

translations.literal: After this came the selecting consort's holding the curtain and hearing government.
translations.idiomatic: After that came the selecting consort hearing government behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 劉遜、李進忠幺麽小豎，何遂膽大揚言。

translations.literal: Liu Xun and Li Jinzong, petty eunuchs, how did they dare speak so boldly?
translations.idiomatic: Petty eunuchs Liu Xun and Li Jinzong—how did they dare speak so boldly?

sentences.zh: 說者謂二豎早以金寶輸從哲家，若非九卿、臺諫力請移宮，選侍一日得誌，陛下幾無駐足所。

translations.literal: Some said the two eunuchs had long since paid gold and jewels into Congzhe's house; had not the nine ministers and censorate and remonstrance officials strenuously asked to move the palace, the selecting consort would in one day have had her way and Your Majesty would scarcely have had a place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the two eunuchs had long bribed Congzhe's household; had not the nine ministers and the remonstrance offices forced the move from the palace, the selecting consort would have had her way in a day and the emperor would scarcely have had footing.

sentences.zh: 聞爾時從哲濡遲不進，科臣趣之，則雲遲數日無害。

translations.literal: It was heard that at the time Congzhe was slow and did not advance; when a section official urged him, he said delay of several days did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: They said Congzhe lingered without acting; when a section official pressed him, he said a few days' delay did no harm.

sentences.zh: 任婦寺之縱橫，忍君父之杌隉，為大臣者宜爾乎？

translations.literal: To let palace women and eunuchs run rampant and bear the peril of ruler and father—should a great minister act thus?
translations.idiomatic: To indulge palace women and eunuchs while ruler and father stood in peril—is that what a great minister should do?

sentences.zh: 臣在禮言禮，其罪惡逆天，萬無可生之路。

translations.literal: Your servant, speaking of rites within the Ministry of Rites, says their crime rebels against Heaven and there is absolutely no path to life.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking as minister of rites, I say their crime rebels against Heaven and leaves no path to life.

sentences.zh: 若其他督戰誤國，罔上行私，縱情蔑法，幹犯天下之名義，釀成國家之禍患者，臣不能悉數也。

translations.literal: As for other matters—urging battle and misleading the state, deceiving the ruler for private ends, indulging passions and despising law, violating the world's right conduct and brewing calamity for the state—your servant cannot enumerate them all.
translations.idiomatic: As for urging war and misleading the state, deceiving the ruler, indulging lawlessness, violating public morality, and brewing national calamity—I cannot list them all.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜急討此賊，雪不共之仇！

translations.literal: Your Majesty should quickly punish this villain and avenge this unshared hatred!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should punish this villain at once and avenge a hatred that cannot be shared!

sentences.zh: 毋詢近習，近習皆從哲所攀援也；

translations.literal: Do not consult those close at hand—those close at hand are all Congzhe's dependents;
translations.idiomatic: Do not heed those close at hand—all are Congzhe's creatures;

sentences.zh: 毋拘忌諱，忌諱即從哲所布置也。

translations.literal: do not be bound by taboos—the taboos are Congzhe's arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: do not be bound by taboos—those taboos are Congzhe's snares.

sentences.zh: 並急誅李可灼，以泄神人之憤。

translations.literal: And quickly execute Li Kezhuo to release the fury of gods and men.
translations.idiomatic: Execute Li Kezhuo at once to appease gods and men.

sentences.zh: 時朝野方惡從哲，慎行論雖過刻，然爭韙其言。

translations.literal: At the time court and countryside alike hated Congzhe; though Shenxing's argument was harsh, men contended in approving his words.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country hated Congzhe; though Shenxing's words were harsh, most approved them.

sentences.zh: 顧近習多為從哲地，帝乃報曰：「舊輔素忠慎，可灼進藥本先帝意。

translations.literal: Yet those close at hand mostly made ground for Congzhe, and the emperor replied: "The former chief minister has always been loyal and cautious; Kezhuo's presenting medicine was originally the late emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Those close at hand mostly shielded Congzhe; the emperor replied: "The former chief minister has always been loyal; Kezhuo's medicine followed the late emperor's wish.

sentences.zh: 卿言雖忠愛，事屬傳聞。

translations.literal: Your words, though loyal and loving, belong to hearsay.
translations.idiomatic: Your words, though loyal, rest on hearsay.

sentences.zh: 並進封移宮事，當日九卿、臺諫官親見者，當據實會奏，用釋群疑。

translations.literal: Together with advancing the matter of moving the palace—on that day the nine ministers and censorate and remonstrance officials who saw it in person should memorialize according to fact to dispel the crowd's doubts."
translations.idiomatic: Together with the move from the palace—let the nine ministers and remonstrators who were present report according to fact and dispel doubt."

sentences.zh: 」於是從哲疏辨。

translations.literal: Thereupon Congzhe memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書黃克纘右從哲，亦曲為辨。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Huang Kexuan sided with Congzhe and also bent the argument in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Huang Kexuan sided with Congzhe and twisted the argument in his favor.

sentences.zh: 慎行復疏折之，曰：「由前則過信可灼，有輕進藥之罪，由後則曲庇可灼，有不討賊之罪，兩者均無辭乎弒也。

translations.literal: Shenxing memorialized again to refute him, saying: "Before, he overtrusted Kezhuo—crime of rashly advancing medicine; after, he bent to shield Kezhuo—crime of not punishing the villain; in both there is no escaping the name of regicide."
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing refuted him again: "Before, he overtrusted Kezhuo—rash medicine; after, he shielded him—failure to punish the villain; either way the charge of regicide stands."

sentences.zh: 從哲謂移宮有揭，但諸臣之請在初二，從哲之請在初五。

translations.literal: Congzhe said there was a memorial on moving the palace, but the gentlemen's request was on the second, Congzhe's on the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe said a memorial on moving the palace existed—but other officials asked on the second, Congzhe on the fifth.

sentences.zh: 爾時章疏入乾清不入慈慶者已三日，國政幾於中斷，非他輔臣訪知，與群臣力請，其害可勝言哉！

translations.literal: By then memorials had entered Qianqing but not Cining for three days and state affairs were nearly cut off; had not other chief ministers learned of it and joined the gentlemen in strenuous request, who can speak of the harm!
translations.idiomatic: For three days memorials entered Qianqing but not Cining; government nearly halted. Had other ministers not learned of it and joined the plea, who can measure the harm!

sentences.zh: 伏讀聖諭『輔臣義在體國，為朕分憂。

translations.literal: I have read the sacred instruction: 'Chief ministers' duty is to embody the state and share Your Majesty's cares.
translations.idiomatic: I read the sacred instruction: 'Chief ministers should embody the state and share Your Majesty's cares.

sentences.zh: 今似此景象，何不代朕傳諭一言，屏息紛擾，君臣大義安在？

translations.literal: Now with a scene like this, why not speak a word for Us to calm the turmoil—where is the great righteousness of ruler and minister?
translations.idiomatic: With turmoil such as this, why not speak one word for Us to calm it—where is ministerial duty?

sentences.zh: 』又雲『朕淩虐不堪，晝夜涕泣六七日。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'We are unbearably abused and have wept day and night for six or seven days.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'We are unbearably abused and have wept six or seven days and nights.'

sentences.zh: 』夫從哲為顧命元臣，使少肯義形於色，何至令至尊憂危如此！

translations.literal: Congzhe as entrusted chief minister—had he only shown a little righteous anger, how could he have let the supreme sovereign be so endangered!
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe as entrusted minister—had he shown righteous anger, how could the sovereign have been driven to such distress!

sentences.zh: 惟阿婦寺之意多，戴聖明之意少，故敢於淩皇祖，悖皇考，而欺陛下也。

translations.literal: He favored palace women and eunuchs too much and honored the sage sovereign too little, and therefore dared to insult the imperial grandfather, wrong the imperial father, and deceive Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: He favored palace creatures over the throne, insulted the imperial grandfather, wronged the imperial father, and deceived Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」末復力言克纘之謬。

translations.literal: At the end he again strenuously set forth Kexuan's error.
translations.idiomatic: He again attacked Kexuan's errors at length.

sentences.zh: 章並下廷議。

translations.literal: The memorials were all sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials went to court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 既而議上，惟可灼下吏戍邊，從哲置不問。

translations.literal: When deliberation was reported, only Kezhuo was sent down to the officials and banished to the frontier; Congzhe was left unquestioned.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation ended with only Kezhuo banished to the frontier; Congzhe went untouched.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫奏，五月中，日中月星並見。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator of Shandong memorialized that in the fifth month sun, moon, and stars appeared together at midday.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's grand coordinator reported sun, moon, and stars visible together at noon in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 慎行以為大異，疏請修省，語極危切。

translations.literal: Shenxing, taking it as a great portent, memorialized asking for self-examination and reform, his words extremely urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing took it as a dire omen and memorialized for repentance in urgent terms.

sentences.zh: 秦王誼漶由旁枝進封，其四子法不當封郡王，厚賄近幸，遂得溫旨。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Huan was enfeoffed from a collateral line; his four sons by law should not be enfeoffed as commandery princes, yet by thick bribes to those close at hand he obtained a mild edict.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Huan, raised from a collateral line, sought commandery-prince titles for four sons contrary to law; heavy bribes to favorites won a mild edict.

sentences.zh: 慎行堅不奉詔，三疏力爭，不得。

translations.literal: Shenxing firmly refused to carry out the edict and contended in three memorials without success.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing refused the edict and protested in three memorials without success.

sentences.zh: 七月謝病去。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 其冬，廷推閣臣，以慎行為首，吏部侍郎盛以弘次之。

translations.literal: That winter, in court nomination for Grand Secretariat members, Shenxing was placed first and Vice Minister of Personnel Sheng Yihong second.
translations.idiomatic: That winter's court nomination for the Grand Secretariat placed Shenxing first and Vice Minister Sheng Yihong second.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢抑不用，用顧秉謙、朱國禎、朱延禧、魏廣微，朝論大駭。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian suppressed them and did not employ them, using Gu Bingqian, Zhu Guozhen, Zhu Yanzhi, and Wei Guangwei; court opinion was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian blocked them and installed Gu Bingqian, Zhu Guozhen, Zhu Yanzhi, and Wei Guangwei instead; court opinion was appalled.

sentences.zh: 葉向高連疏請用兩人，竟不得命。

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao submitted successive memorials asking to employ the two men, yet in the end received no order.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao repeatedly asked that the two be appointed, but no order came.

sentences.zh: 已，忠賢大熾，議修《三朝要典》，「紅丸」之案以慎行為罪魁。

translations.literal: Later Zhongxian grew greatly powerful and deliberated compiling the 《Essentials of the Three Reigns》; in the "red pill" case Shenxing was made the arch-culprit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian grew all-powerful, compilers of the 《Essentials of the Three Reigns》 made Shenxing the arch-culprit in the red-pill affair.

sentences.zh: 其黨張訥遂上疏力詆，有詔削奪。

translations.literal: His partisan Zhang Na thereupon memorialized attacking with force; an edict stripped his honors.
translations.idiomatic: Partisan Zhang Na attacked him fiercely; an edict stripped his honors.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劉誌選復兩疏追劾，詔撫按提問，遣戍寧夏。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Zhixuan again impeached him in two memorials; an edict ordered the grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner to interrogate and sent him into banishment in Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Zhixuan impeached him again; an edict ordered provincial interrogation and banishment to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 未行，莊烈帝嗣位，以赦免。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded; he was pardoned by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded and amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，命以故官協理詹事府，力辭不就。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was ordered to his former office to assist in the Directorate of the Heir Apparent but strenuously declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he was ordered to assist the Directorate of the Heir Apparent at his former rank but declined.

sentences.zh: 慎行操行峻潔，為一時搢紳冠。

translations.literal: Shenxing's conduct was stern and pure; he was the crown of gentry of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing's conduct was stern and pure; gentry of the age ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 朝士數推轂入閣，吏部尚書王永光力排之，迄不獲用。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen repeatedly pushed him into the Grand Secretariat; Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang strenuously blocked him, and in the end he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers repeatedly urged his appointment to the Grand Secretariat; Minister Wang Yongguang blocked him, and he was never used.

sentences.zh: 八年廷推閣臣，屢不稱旨，最後以慎行及劉宗周、林釬名上，帝即召之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, in court nomination for Grand Secretariat members, several times it did not please the emperor; at last Shenxing, Liu Zongzhou, and Lin Qian were named; the emperor at once summoned them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, court nominations for the Grand Secretariat repeatedly failed to please the emperor; at last Shenxing, Liu Zongzhou, and Lin Qian were named and summoned.

sentences.zh: 慎行已得疾，甫入都，卒。

translations.literal: Shenxing was already ill; he had just entered the capital when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing was already ill; he died soon after reaching the capital.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文介。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent with the posthumous name Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 盛以弘，字子寬，潼關衛人。

translations.literal: Sheng Yihong, styled Zikuan, was a man of Tongguan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yihong, whose style name was Zikuan, came from Tongguan Guard.

sentences.zh: 父訥，字敏叔。

translations.literal: His father Ne, styled Minshu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng Ne, styled Minshu.

sentences.zh: 訥父德，世職指揮也，討洛南盜戰死。

translations.literal: Ne's father De held the hereditary post of commander; campaigning against bandits in Luonan he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's father De held a hereditary commander's post and died fighting bandits in Luonan.

sentences.zh: 訥號泣請於當事，水漿不入口者數日，為發兵討斬之。

translations.literal: Ne wailed and begged those in power; for several days he would not take water or food, and troops were sent to pursue and behead the killers.
translations.idiomatic: Ne wailed and begged the authorities; for days he took no food or drink until troops were sent to hunt down and kill the bandits.

sentences.zh: 久之，舉隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: After a long time he became a jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he became a jinshi in Longqing 5.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士累官吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: From Academician Reader he rose successively to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin academician reader he rose to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 與尚書陳有年、左侍郎趙參魯共厘銓政。

translations.literal: Together with Minister Chen Younian and Left Vice Minister Zhao Canlu he rectified appointment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With Minister Chen Younian and Left Vice Minister Zhao Canlu he reformed appointments.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，以篤孝聞。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning and was known for deep filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his mother's mourning and was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，謚文定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was given the posthumous name Wending.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he received the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: 以弘，萬歷二十六年進士。

translations.literal: Yihong became a jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Yihong became a jinshi in Wanli 26.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士累官禮部尚書。

translations.literal: From Academician Reader he rose successively to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin academician reader he rose to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年謝病歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi he resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 3 he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢亂政，落其職。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian disturbed government, his post was removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian seized power, his post was stripped.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起故官，協理詹事府，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was raised to his former office to assist the Directorate of the Heir Apparent and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he was restored to assist the Directorate of the Heir Apparent and died in office.

sentences.zh: 明世，衛所世職用儒業顯者，訥父子而已。

translations.literal: In the Ming dynasty, among hereditary guard posts made illustrious through Confucian learning, only the father and son Ne were such.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming times, only the Ne father and son among hereditary guards won fame through Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 高攀龍，字存之，無錫人。

translations.literal: Gao Panlong, styled Cunzhi, was a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Panlong, whose style name was Cunzhi, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，輒有誌程朱之學。

translations.literal: In youth when he read books he at once set his will on the learning of Cheng and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: From youth, whenever he read, he resolved to follow the learning of Cheng and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷十七年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi and was appointed Courier.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 17 he became a jinshi and was appointed courier.

sentences.zh: 四川僉事張世則進所著《大學初義》，詆程、朱章句，請頒天下。

translations.literal: Sichuan Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhang Shize presented his 《Initial Meaning of the Great Learning》, slandering the chapter-and-phrase learning of Cheng and Zhu, and asked that it be issued throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shize, assistant administration commissioner of Sichuan, submitted his 《Initial Meaning of the Great Learning》, attacking Cheng-Zhu exegesis, and asked that it be promulgated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 攀龍抗疏力駁其謬，其書遂不行。

translations.literal: Panlong submitted a stern memorial refuting its error, and the book was not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong refuted it in a fierce memorial, and the book was not issued.

sentences.zh: 侍郎趙用賢、都御史李世達被訐去位，朝論多咎大學士王錫爵。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhao Yongxian and Censor-in-Chief Li Shida were impeached and left office; court opinion largely blamed Grand Secretary Wang Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhao Yongxian and censor-in-chief Li Shida were driven out; court opinion largely blamed Grand Secretary Wang Xijue.

sentences.zh: 攀龍上疏曰：

translations.literal: Panlong memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Panlong memorialized:

sentences.zh: 近見朝寧之上，善類擯斥一空。

translations.literal: Recently on the morning court the ranks of the good have been swept away empty.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the good have been swept from court.

sentences.zh: 大臣則孫鑨、李世達、趙用賢去矣，小臣則趙南星、陳泰來、顧允成、薛敷教、張納陛、於孔兼、賈巖斥矣。

translations.literal: Among great ministers Sun Lu, Li Shida, and Zhao Yongxian have gone; among lesser officials Zhao Nanxing, Chen Tailai, Gu Yuncheng, Xue Fujiao, Zhang Nalu, Yu Kongjian, and Jia Yan have been expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers Sun Lu, Li Shida, and Zhao Yongxian are gone; lesser officials Zhao Nanxing, Chen Tailai, Gu Yuncheng, Xue Fujiao, Zhang Nalu, Yu Kongjian, and Jia Yan have been expelled.

sentences.zh: 邇者李禎、曾乾亨復不安其位而乞去矣，選郎孟化鯉又以推用言官張棟，空署而逐矣。

translations.literal: Recently Li Zhen and Zeng Qianheng again could not rest secure in their posts and begged to leave; Appointments Director Meng Huayu, because he recommended remonstrance official Zhang Dong, was left with an empty title and driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Li Zhen and Zeng Qianheng could not hold their posts and begged leave; appointments director Meng Huayu, for recommending remonstrator Zhang Dong, was left titular and driven out.

sentences.zh: 夫天地生才甚難，國家需才甚亟，廢斥如此，後將焉繼。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth produce talent with great difficulty; the state needs talent with great urgency—dismissal on this scale, who will follow after?
translations.idiomatic: Talent is hard for heaven and earth to produce and the state urgently needs it—dismiss so many, and who remains?

sentences.zh: 致使正人扼腕，曲士彈冠，世道人心何可勝慨！

translations.literal: It makes upright men wring their hands and crooked men don their caps—how can the way of the world and the hearts of men be fully lamented!
translations.idiomatic: Upright men wring their hands while crooked men rejoice—what lament can suffice for the age!

sentences.zh: 且今陛下朝講久輟，廷臣不獲望見顏色。

translations.literal: Moreover, today Your Majesty's morning lectures have long ceased, and court ministers cannot behold your countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, morning lectures have long ceased and ministers cannot see your face.

sentences.zh: 天言傳布，雖曰聖裁，隱伏之中，莫測所以。

translations.literal: Heaven's words are transmitted and issued; though called the sacred decision, in what is hidden none can measure the source.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial words are issued as sacred decisions, yet none can trace their hidden source.

sentences.zh: 故中外群言，不曰：「輔臣欲除不附己」，則曰「近侍不利用正人」。

translations.literal: Therefore talk inside and outside alike does not say 'the chief ministers wish to remove those who do not attach to themselves,' but says 'those close at hand cannot use upright men.'
translations.idiomatic: So rumor says not that chief ministers purge dissenters, but that those close at hand cannot abide upright men.

sentences.zh: 陛下深居九重，亦曾有以諸臣賢否陳於左右；

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells deep in the ninefold palace—have you ever had whether the gentlemen are worthy or not reported at your side;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells deep within the palace—has anyone reported which ministers are worthy?

sentences.zh: 而陛下於諸臣，亦嘗一思其得罪之故乎？

translations.literal: and have you ever once pondered the reason for their punishment?
translations.idiomatic: Have you pondered why they were punished?

sentences.zh: 果以為皆由聖怒，則諸臣自孟化鯉而外，未聞忤旨，何以皆罷斥？

translations.literal: If truly you think it is all from sacred anger, then apart from Meng Huayu none are heard to have offended the edict—why are all dismissed?
translations.idiomatic: If all were punished by your anger, apart from Meng Huayu none offended the throne—why are all dismissed?

sentences.zh: 即使批鱗逆耳，如董基等，陛下已嘗收錄，何獨於諸臣不然？

translations.literal: Even if they were scales-ripping and ear-offending, like Dong Ji and others whom Your Majesty has already taken back, why are these gentlemen not treated the same?
translations.idiomatic: Even when remonstrators offended, as with Dong Ji whom you recalled, why not these men?

sentences.zh: 臣恐陛下有祛邪之果斷，而左右反借以行冒嫉之私；

translations.literal: Your servant fears Your Majesty has the resolute fruit of expelling evil, yet those at your side borrow it to pursue private envy;
translations.idiomatic: I fear you have resolve to expel evil, yet those at your side use it for private envy;

sentences.zh: 陛下有容言之盛心，而臣工反遺以拒諫諍之誚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has a magnanimous heart willing to hear words, yet ministers leave behind the shame of rejecting remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: you have a heart willing to hear words, yet ministers earn the shame of rejecting remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 傳之四海，垂諸史冊，為聖德累不小。

translations.literal: Transmit this to the four seas and fix it in the historical records—the burden on sagely virtue is not small.
translations.idiomatic: Spread abroad and fix in history, the burden on your sacred virtue is not small.

sentences.zh: 輔臣王錫爵等，跡其自待，若愈於張居正、申時行，察其用心，何以異於五十步笑百步？

translations.literal: Chief Minister Wang Xijue and others—in their self-regard they seem better than Zhang Juzheng and Shen Shixing, yet examine their intent—how does it differ from laughing at a man fifty paces away while being a hundred paces away?
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Wang Xijue and others seem better than Zhang Juzheng and Shen Shixing in manner, yet in intent differ only as fifty paces from a hundred.

sentences.zh: 即如諸臣罷斥，果以為當然，則是非邪正，恒人能辨，何忍坐視至尊之過舉，得毋內泄其私憤，而利於斥逐之盡乎？

translations.literal: As for the gentlemen's dismissal, if truly thought fitting, then right and wrong the ordinary man can distinguish—how can one bear to sit and watch the supreme sovereign's mistaken measures? Can it be other than leaking private resentment within and profiting from their thorough expulsion?
translations.idiomatic: If their dismissal were just, any man could see right from wrong—how bear to watch your mistaken measures? Is it not private resentment profiting from their expulsion?

sentences.zh: 末力詆鄭材、楊應宿讒諂宜黜。

translations.literal: At the end he strenuously denounced Zheng Cai and Yang Yingsu for slander and flattery and said they should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He ended by demanding dismissal of Zheng Cai and Yang Yingsu for slander and flattery.

sentences.zh: 應宿亦疏訐攀龍，語極妄誕。

translations.literal: Yingsu also memorialized attacking Panlong with words extremely wild and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsu attacked Panlong in turn with absurd charges.

sentences.zh: 疏並下部院，議請薄罰兩臣，稍示懲創。

translations.literal: The memorials were sent together to the ministries and the censorate; deliberation asked a light punishment for the two gentlemen to show some correction.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials went to the ministries; deliberation proposed light punishment for both.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，鐫應宿二秩，謫攀龍揭陽添註典史。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it; Yingsu's rank was reduced two steps and Panlong was banished to Jieyang as an added Registry Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; Yingsu was reduced two ranks and Panlong banished to Jieyang as registry clerk.

sentences.zh: 御史吳弘濟等論救，並獲譴。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Hongji and others pleaded in defense and were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wu Hongji and others who pleaded for him were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 攀龍之官七月，以事歸。

translations.literal: Panlong had been in office seven months and returned home on business.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong had served seven months and returned home on business.

sentences.zh: 尋遭親喪，遂不出，家居垂三十年。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered his father's mourning and did not go out again, living at home for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his father and did not return, living at home nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 言者屢薦，帝悉不省。

translations.literal: Remonstrators repeatedly recommended him; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators repeatedly recommended him; the emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 熹宗立，起光祿丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended, he was raised Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong took the throne, he was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Banquets.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年進少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he was advanced Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1 he was promoted vice minister.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，疏劾戚畹鄭養性，言：「張差梃擊實養性父國泰主謀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year he memorialized impeaching the imperial consort's kinsman Zheng Yangxing, saying: "Zhang Chai's staff attack was in truth masterminded by Yangxing's father Guotai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year he impeached imperial kinsman Zheng Yangxing, writing: "Zhang Chai's assault was masterminded by Yangxing's father Guotai.

sentences.zh: 今人言籍籍，鹹疑養性交關奸宄，別懷異謀，積疑不解，當思善全之術。

translations.literal: Now men's talk is clamorous; all suspect Yangxing of contact with traitors and separate sinister designs; accumulated suspicion unresolved, one should think of means to preserve him whole.
translations.idiomatic: Talk is clamorous; many suspect Yangxing of dealing with traitors—suspicion unresolved, means should be found to protect him.

sentences.zh: 至劉保謀逆，中官盧受主之，劉於簡獄詞具在。

translations.literal: As for Liu Bao's plot of rebellion, palace eunuch Lu Shou was behind it; Liu's confession in the prison interrogation is fully there.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bao's rebellion was directed by palace eunuch Lu Shou, as Liu's confession shows.

sentences.zh: 受本鄭氏私人，而李如楨一家交關鄭氏，計陷名將，失地喪師。

translations.literal: Shou was originally the Zheng family's private man, and the Li Ruzhen family trafficked with the Zheng family, scheming to frame a famous general and lose territory and troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was the Zheng family's man; the Li Ruzhen family colluded with the Zhengs, framed a famous general, and lost territory and troops.

sentences.zh: 於簡原供，明言李永芳約如楨內應。

translations.literal: In the original confession it clearly states Li Yongfang agreed to respond inside at Ruzhen's signal.
translations.idiomatic: The confession states plainly that Li Yongfang agreed to respond within at Ruzhen's signal.

sentences.zh: 若崔文升素為鄭氏腹心，知先帝癥虛，故用泄藥，罪在不赦。

translations.literal: As for Cui Wensheng, he was long the Zheng family's trusted man; knowing the late emperor's illness was weak, he therefore used a purging medicine—crime unpardonable.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wensheng, long the Zheng family's confidant, knowing the late emperor's weakness, used a purging medicine—a crime unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 陛下僅行斥逐，而文升猶潛住都城。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has only carried out expulsion, yet Wensheng still secretly dwells in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty expelled him, yet Wensheng still lurks in the capital.

sentences.zh: 宜勒養性還故裏，急正如楨、文升典刑，用章國法。

translations.literal: Yangxing should be ordered to return to his native place, and Ruzhen and Wensheng should quickly be punished according to law to manifest the state's law.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing should be sent home; Ruzhen and Wensheng should be punished at once to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，責攀龍多言，然卒遣養性還籍。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Panlong was rebuked for speaking too much, yet in the end Yangxing was sent back to his register.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial drew rebuke for speaking too much, yet Yangxing was still sent home.

sentences.zh: 孫慎行以「紅丸」事攻舊輔方從哲，下廷議。

translations.literal: Sun Shenxing attacked former chief minister Fang Congzhe over the "red pill" affair, and it was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shenxing attacked former chief minister Fang Congzhe over the red-pill affair, and the case went to court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 攀龍引《春秋》首惡之誅，歸獄從哲。

translations.literal: Panlong cited the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 on punishing the chief villain and placed guilt on Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong cited the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 on punishing the chief villain and laid guilt on Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 給事中王誌道為從哲解，攀龍遺書切責之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Zhidao defended Congzhe; Panlong left a letter sternly rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Zhidao defended Congzhe; Panlong sent a letter rebuking him sharply.

sentences.zh: 尋改太常少卿，疏陳務學之要，因言：「從哲之罪非止紅丸，其最大者在交結鄭國泰。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized on the essentials of pursuing learning, saying: "Congzhe's crimes are not limited to the red pill; the greatest lies in his collusion with Zheng Guotai.
translations.idiomatic: Made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he memorialized on learning and wrote: "Congzhe's crimes exceed the red pill; the greatest was collusion with Zheng Guotai.

sentences.zh: 國泰父子所以謀危先帝者不一，始以張差之梃，繼以美姝之進，終以文升之藥，而從哲實左右之。

translations.literal: The means by which Guotai father and son plotted to endanger the late emperor were not one: first the staff of Zhang Chai, next the entry of beautiful women, finally Wensheng's medicine—and Congzhe was truly at their side.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai father and son endangered the late emperor step by step—Zhang Chai's staff, beautiful women, Wensheng's medicine—and Congzhe stood at their side.

sentences.zh: 力扶其為鄭氏者，力鋤其不為鄭氏者；

translations.literal: Those who strenuously supported the Zheng faction and strenuously uprooted those who would not serve the Zheng faction—
translations.idiomatic: He backed the Zheng faction and uprooted all who would not;

sentences.zh: 一時人心若狂，但知鄭氏，不知東宮。

translations.literal: for a time men's hearts were mad and knew only the Zheng family, not the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: for a time men knew only the Zheng name, not the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 此賊臣也，討賊則為陛下之孝。

translations.literal: This is a treacherous minister; to punish the villain is filial piety toward Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: This is treason; to punish the villain is filial service to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 而說者乃曰『為先帝隱諱則為孝』，此大亂之道也。

translations.literal: Yet some say 'to spare the late emperor's name is filial piety'—this is the way of great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some say sparing the late emperor's name is filial—that is the road to chaos.

sentences.zh: 陛下念聖母則宣選侍之罪，念皇考則隆選侍之恩，仁之至義之盡也，而說者乃曰『為聖母隱諱則為孝』。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, mindful of the sage mother, should proclaim the selecting consort's crime; mindful of the imperial father, should honor the selecting consort's grace—the utmost of benevolence and righteousness—yet some say 'to spare the sage mother is filial piety.'
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the empress dowager, proclaim the selecting consort's crime; mindful of your father, honor her as duty requires—yet some call that unfilial.

sentences.zh: 明如聖諭，目為假托；

translations.literal: As clear as the sacred instruction, they call it false pretense;
translations.idiomatic: Clear imperial words they call false pretense;

sentences.zh: 忠如楊漣，謗為居功。

translations.literal: as loyal as Yang Lian, they slander as courting merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lian's loyalty they call self-promotion.

sentences.zh: 人臣避居功，甘居罪，君父有急，袖手旁觀，此大亂之道也。

translations.literal: Ministers avoid merit and are content with guilt; when ruler and father are in peril they stand by with folded sleeves—this is the way of great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers shun merit and accept guilt; when ruler and father are in peril they stand aside—that is chaos.

sentences.zh: 惑於其說，孝也不知其為孝，不孝也以為大孝；

translations.literal: Bewitched by such talk, filial piety is not known as filial piety, and unfilial conduct is thought great filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: Under such talk, filial piety is not recognized as filial, and unfilial conduct is called great filial piety;

sentences.zh: 忠也不知其為忠，不忠也以為大忠。

translations.literal: loyalty is not known as loyalty, and disloyalty is thought great loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty is not recognized as loyal, and disloyalty is called great loyalty.

sentences.zh: 忠孝皆可變亂，何事不可妄為？

translations.literal: If loyalty and filial piety can both be turned to disorder, what cannot be rashly done?
translations.idiomatic: If loyalty and filial piety can be twisted into chaos, what may not be done?

sentences.zh: 故從哲、養性不容不討，奈何猶令居輦轂下！

translations.literal: Therefore Congzhe and Yangxing cannot escape punishment—why are they still allowed to dwell beneath the imperial chariot!
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe and Yangxing cannot go unpunished—why do they still dwell near the throne!

sentences.zh: 」時從哲輩奧援甚固，摘疏中「不孝」語激帝怒，將加嚴譴。

translations.literal: At the time Congzhe's factional support was very solid; seizing the word "unfilial" in the memorial provoked the emperor's anger and severe punishment was about to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe's faction was strong; the word "unfilial" in the memorial enraged the emperor and severe punishment loomed.

sentences.zh: 葉向高力救，乃奪祿一年。

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao rescued him strenuously, and he was fined one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao pleaded hard, and he was fined one year's salary.

sentences.zh: 旋改大理少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 鄒元標建書院，攀龍與焉。

translations.literal: Zou Yuanbiao founded the academy; Panlong joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yuanbiao founded the academy, and Panlong joined him.

sentences.zh: 元標被攻，攀龍請與同罷，詔留之。

translations.literal: When Yuanbiao was attacked, Panlong asked to resign with him; an edict retained him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanbiao was attacked, Panlong asked to resign with him but was ordered to stay.

sentences.zh: 進太仆卿，擢刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and promoted Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and then vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，拜左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year he was appointed left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 楊漣等群擊魏忠賢，勢已不兩立。

translations.literal: Yang Lian and others together attacked Wei Zhongxian; the situation was already irreconcilable.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lian and others attacked Wei Zhongxian together; the breach was irreparable.

sentences.zh: 及向高去國，魏廣微日導忠賢為惡，而攀龍為趙南星門生，並居要地。

translations.literal: When Xianggao left the state, Wei Guangwei daily guided Zhongxian in evil, while Panlong as Zhao Nanxing's student also held a key post.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianggao left office, Wei Guangwei daily led Zhongxian deeper into evil, while Panlong, Nanxing's student, held a key post.

sentences.zh: 御史崔呈秀按淮、揚還，攀龍發其穢狀，南星議戍之。

translations.literal: Censor Cui Chengxiu, returning from inspecting Huai and Yang, had his filthy conduct exposed by Panlong; Nanxing proposed banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cui Chengxiu, returning from Huai-Yang inspection, had his corruption exposed by Panlong; Nanxing proposed banishment.

sentences.zh: 呈秀窘，急走忠賢所，乞為義兒，遂摭謝應祥事，謂攀龍黨南星。

translations.literal: Chengxiu was cornered, ran in haste to Zhongxian's place, begged to become his adopted son, and thereupon seized on the Xie Yingxiang affair, saying Panlong was Nanxing's partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Chengxiu fled to Zhongxian, begged to become his adopted son, and seized on the Xie Yingxiang affair to call Panlong Nanxing's partisan.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨詰責，攀龍遽引罪去。

translations.literal: A stern edict rebuked him; Panlong hastily took blame and left.
translations.idiomatic: A stern edict rebuked him; Panlong took blame and resigned.

sentences.zh: 頃之，南京御史遊鳳翔出為知府，訐攀龍挾私排擠。

translations.literal: Before long Nanjing Censor You Fengxiang went out as prefect and accused Panlong of using private spite to drive men out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nanjing censor You Fengxiang, sent out as prefect, accused Panlong of driving men out from private spite.

sentences.zh: 詔復鳳翔故官，削攀龍籍。

translations.literal: An edict restored Fengxiang to his former office and struck Panlong from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Fengxiang and struck Panlong from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 呈秀憾不已，必欲殺之，竄名李實劾周起元疏中，遣緹騎往逮。

translations.literal: Chengxiu's hatred was still unappeased and he was determined to kill him; he inserted Panlong's name in Censor Li Shi's memorial impeaching Zhou Qiyuan and sent imperial guards to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu's hatred was unslaked; he inserted Panlong's name in Li Shi's memorial against Zhou Qiyuan and sent guards to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 攀龍晨謁宋儒楊龜山祠，以文告之。

translations.literal: Panlong in the morning paid respects at the shrine of the Song Confucian Yang Guishan and addressed him in a literary notice.
translations.idiomatic: That morning Panlong visited the shrine of the Song scholar Yang Guishan and addressed him in a written prayer.

sentences.zh: 歸與二門生一弟飲後園池上，聞周順昌已就逮，笑曰：「吾視死如歸，今果然矣。

translations.literal: Returning, he drank with two students and a younger brother by the rear garden pool; hearing Zhou Shunchang had been arrested, he smiled and said: "I regard death as going home; today it is truly so.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he drank with two students and a younger brother by the garden pool; hearing Zhou Shunchang had been arrested, he smiled: "I regarded death as going home; today it is so.

sentences.zh: 」入與夫人語，如平時。

translations.literal: He entered and spoke with his wife as at ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with his wife as on any ordinary day.

sentences.zh: 出，書二紙告二孫曰：「明日以付官校。

translations.literal: Coming out, he wrote two sheets and told his two grandsons: "Tomorrow give these to the official guards.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote two sheets for his grandsons: "Give these to the guards tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」因遣之出，扃戶。

translations.literal: He then sent them out and barred the door.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sent them out and barred the door.

sentences.zh: 移時諸子排戶入，一燈熒然，則已衣冠自沈於池矣。

translations.literal: After a time the sons broke in the door; a single lamp burned dimly—he had already donned his cap and robes and drowned himself in the pool.
translations.idiomatic: When his sons broke in, a single lamp still burned—he had donned cap and robes and drowned himself in the pool.

sentences.zh: 發所封紙，乃遺表也，云：「臣雖削奪，舊為大臣，大臣受辱則辱國。

translations.literal: Opening the sealed papers, it was a final memorial, saying: "Your servant, though stripped of honors, was formerly a great minister; when a great minister is shamed, the state is shamed.
translations.idiomatic: The sealed papers were a final memorial: "Though stripped of rank, I was a great minister; when a minister is shamed, the state is shamed.

sentences.zh: 謹北向叩頭，從屈平之遺則。

translations.literal: Respectfully kowtowing northward, I follow Qu Ping's legacy."
translations.idiomatic: I kowtow northward and follow Qu Yuan's example."

sentences.zh: 」復別門人華允誠書云：「一生學問，至此亦少得力。

translations.literal: He also left a separate letter to his student Hua Yuncheng: "A lifetime of learning—at this point one gains a little power."
translations.idiomatic: To his student Hua Yuncheng he wrote: "A lifetime of learning—here at last it proves its worth."

sentences.zh: 」時年六十五。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-five sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞其死，莫不傷之。

translations.literal: Near and far, hearing of his death, none did not grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far, all grieved his death.

sentences.zh: 呈秀憾猶未釋，矯詔下其子世儒吏。

translations.literal: Chengxiu's hatred was still unappeased; a forged edict sent his son Shiru to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu's hatred endured; a forged edict sent his son Shiru before the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 刑部坐世儒不能防閑其父，謫為徒。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice convicted Shiru for failing to restrain his father and banished him as a convict laborer.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice convicted Shiru for failing to restrain his father and sentenced him to convict labor.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太子少保，兵部尚書，謚忠憲，授世儒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War with the posthumous name Zhongxian, and Shiru was given office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent and minister of war with the posthumous name Zhongxian; Shiru received an office.

sentences.zh: 初，海內學者率宗王守仁，攀龍心非之。

translations.literal: Earlier, scholars throughout the realm mostly honored Wang Shouren; Panlong inwardly disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, scholars empire-wide mostly followed Wang Yangming; Panlong inwardly disagreed.

sentences.zh: 與顧憲成同講學東林書院，以靜為主。

translations.literal: Together with Gu Xiancheng he lectured at the Donglin Academy, taking stillness as the main principle.
translations.idiomatic: With Gu Xiancheng he taught at the Donglin Academy, taking stillness as the core.

sentences.zh: 操履篤實，粹然一出於正，為一時儒者之宗。

translations.literal: His conduct was solid and sincere, purely emerging from the upright, and he was patriarch of Confucians of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was solid and sincere, wholly upright, and he was patriarch of the age's Confucians.

sentences.zh: 海內士大夫，識與不識，稱高、顧無異詞。

translations.literal: Gentry throughout the realm, whether they knew him or not, spoke of Gao and Gu without differing words.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere, knowing him or not, spoke of Gao and Gu with one voice.

sentences.zh: 攀龍削官之秋，詔毀東林書院。

translations.literal: In the autumn when Panlong was struck from office, an edict ordered the Donglin Academy destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Panlong was struck from office, an edict ordered the Donglin Academy destroyed.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，學者更修復之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded, scholars restored it again.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded, scholars restored it.

sentences.zh: 馮從吾，字仲好，長安人。

translations.literal: Feng Congwu, styled Zhonghao, was a man of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Congwu, whose style name was Zhonghao, came from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Wanli 17.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Academician Reader and appointed Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin academician reader and was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 巡視中城，閹人修刺謁，拒卻之。

translations.literal: Inspecting the inner city, eunuchs came to pay respects and offer bribes; he refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolling the inner city, he refused eunuchs who came with bribes.

sentences.zh: 禮科都給事中胡汝寧傾邪狡猾，累劾不去。

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary of the Rites Section Hu Runing was perverse and crafty; though repeatedly impeached he did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Chief supervising secretary of the rites section Hu Runing was crooked; though repeatedly impeached he would not go.

sentences.zh: 從吾發其奸，遂調外。

translations.literal: Congwu exposed his wickedness, and he was transferred abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Congwu exposed his crimes and he was transferred out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 時當大計，從吾嚴邏偵，苞苴絕跡。

translations.literal: At the time came the great review; Congwu strictly patrolled the roads and gift-giving vanished.
translations.idiomatic: During the great review Congwu patrolled strictly and bribery ceased.

sentences.zh: 二十年正月，抗章言：「陛下郊廟不親，朝講不禦，章奏留中不發。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twentieth year he submitted a stern memorial saying: "Your Majesty does not personally attend the suburban sacrifices and temple offerings, does not hold morning lectures, and holds memorials in abeyance without issuing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 20 he memorialized sternly: "Your Majesty does not attend sacrifices, does not hold morning lectures, and holds memorials without reply.

sentences.zh: 試觀戊子以前，四裔效順，海不揚波；

translations.literal: Consider before the wuzi year—the four barbarians submitted and the sea did not raise waves;
translations.idiomatic: Before the wuzi year the four quarters submitted and the sea was calm;

sentences.zh: 己丑以後，南倭告警，北寇渝盟，天變人妖，疊出累告。

translations.literal: after the jichou year, Japanese pirates on the south gave alarm and northern enemies broke the alliance; heavenly changes and human prodigies piled up in repeated reports.
translations.idiomatic: after jichou, Japanese pirates alarmed the south and northern enemies broke treaty; omens multiplied.

sentences.zh: 勵精之效如彼，怠斁之患如此。

translations.literal: The effect of striving for refinement was like that; the harm of slackness is like this.
translations.idiomatic: The fruit of diligence was peace; the fruit of slackness is peril.

sentences.zh: 近頌敕諭，謂聖體違和，欲借此自掩，不知鼓鐘於宮，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Recently an edict of instruction was praised, saying the sacred person is unwell and wishes to use this to cover himself—not knowing that when drums and bells sound in the palace, the sound is heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: A recent edict claimed ill health to cover indulgence—not knowing palace drums are heard outside.

sentences.zh: 陛下每夕必飲，每飲必醉，每醉必怒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty every evening must drink, every drinking must become drunk, every drunkenness must become anger.
translations.idiomatic: Every evening you drink, every drinking ends in drunkenness, every drunkenness in rage.

sentences.zh: 左右一言稍違，輒斃杖下，外庭無不知者。

translations.literal: If those at your side speak one word slightly against you, they are beaten to death under the staff; the outer court knows it all.
translations.idiomatic: One word from those at your side brings death by staff; the outer court knows all.

sentences.zh: 天下後世，其可欺乎！

translations.literal: Can the world and later ages be deceived!
translations.idiomatic: Can you deceive the world and posterity!

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿以天變為不足畏，勿以人言為不足恤，勿以目前晏安為可恃，勿以將來危亂為可忽，宗社幸甚。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty not to think heavenly changes insufficient to fear, not to think human words insufficient to heed, not to think present peace and security dependable, not to think future peril and disorder negligible—the altars of state would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Do not think omens unworthy of fear, public talk unworthy of heed, present ease secure, or future peril remote—the dynasty would be blessed.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，欲廷杖之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and wished to beat him at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and meant to beat him at court.

sentences.zh: 會仁聖太后壽辰，閣臣力解得免。

translations.literal: It happened to be the birthday of the Ren Sheng Empress Dowager; chief ministers strenuously interceded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: It was the Ren Sheng empress dowager's birthday; chief ministers interceded and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸，起巡長蘆鹽政。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to return home and was raised to inspect the Changlu salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire and was appointed to inspect the Changlu salt administration.

sentences.zh: 潔己惠商，奸宄斂跡。

translations.literal: He kept himself pure and favored merchants; traitors and villains drew in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: He kept himself pure, favored honest trade, and criminals shrank back.

sentences.zh: 既還朝，適帝以軍政大黜兩京言官。

translations.literal: When he returned to court, it happened that the emperor on military grounds greatly dismissed remonstrance officials of both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor dismissed remonstrance officials of both capitals on military grounds.

sentences.zh: 從吾亦削籍，猶以前疏故也。

translations.literal: Congwu was also struck from the rolls—still because of the earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Congwu was struck from the rolls as well—still for the earlier memorial.

sentences.zh: 從吾生而純愨，長誌濂、洛之學，受業許孚遠。

translations.literal: Congwu was pure and sincere by nature; from youth he set his will on the learning of Zhou Dunyi and Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi, studying under Xu Fuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Congwu was pure by nature; from youth he devoted himself to the learning of Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers under Xu Fuyuan.

sentences.zh: 罷官歸，杜門謝客，取先正格言，體驗身心，造詣益邃。

translations.literal: Dismissed from office, he shut his door to guests, took the sayings of former worthies, tested them in body and mind, and his attainment grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed, he shut his door, tested former worthies' sayings in his own person, and deepened his attainment.

sentences.zh: 家居二十五年。

translations.literal: He lived at home twenty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home twenty-five years.

sentences.zh: 光宗踐阼，起尚寶卿，進太仆少卿，並以兄喪未赴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was raised Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals and advanced Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, but because of his elder brother's mourning he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended he was made vice minister of seals and of the imperial stud, but did not go because of his brother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 俄改大理。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he was promoted left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 甫兩月，進左副都御史。

translations.literal: Barely two months later he was advanced Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Barely two months later he was made left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 廷議「三安」，從吾言：「李可灼以至尊嘗試，而許其引疾，當國何心！

translations.literal: In court deliberation on the "three pacifications," Congwu said: "Li Kezhuo was permitted to retire citing illness after testing medicine on the supreme sovereign—what was the mind of those who held the state!
translations.idiomatic: In deliberation on the "three pacifications," Congwu said: "Li Kezhuo was allowed to retire after testing medicine on the sovereign—what mind ruled the state!

sentences.zh: 至梃擊之獄，與發奸諸臣為難者，即奸人也。

translations.literal: As for the staff-assault case, those who make difficulty for the gentlemen who exposed the villain are themselves villains."
translations.idiomatic: In the staff-assault case, those who trouble the men who exposed the villain are villains themselves."

sentences.zh: 」由是群小惡之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the petty men hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The petty men hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 已，與鄒元標共建首善書院，集同誌講學其中，給事中朱童蒙遂疏詆之。

translations.literal: Later he and Zou Yuanbiao together founded the Shou Shan Academy and gathered like-minded men to lecture there; Supervising Secretary Zhu Tongmeng thereupon memorialized to denounce them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Zou Yuanbiao founded the Shou Shan Academy; Zhu Tongmeng denounced them.

sentences.zh: 從吾言：「宋之不競，以禁講學故，非以講學故也。

translations.literal: Congwu said: "The Song dynasty's failure to compete came from forbidding lecturing, not from lecturing itself.
translations.idiomatic: Congwu wrote: "The Song fell because lecturing was forbidden, not because it was practiced.

sentences.zh: 我二祖表章《六經》，天子經筵，皇太子出閣，皆講學也。

translations.literal: Our two founders exalted the 《Six Classics》; the Son of Heaven's classics lecture, the heir apparent's emergence from the palace—all are lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperors exalted the 《Six Classics》; the sovereign's classics lecture and the heir apparent's schooling are lecturing.

sentences.zh: 臣子以此望君，而己則不為，可乎？

translations.literal: Ministers look to the ruler with this, yet will not do it themselves—can it be?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers expect this of the ruler yet refuse it themselves—can that stand?

sentences.zh: 先臣守仁，當兵事倥傯，不廢講學，卒成大功。

translations.literal: Former minister Shouren, amid urgent military affairs, did not cease lecturing and in the end achieved great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yangming, amid war, did not cease lecturing and achieved great merit.

sentences.zh: 此臣等所以不恤毀譽，而為此也。

translations.literal: This is why your servant and others do not spare reputation and do this."
translations.idiomatic: That is why we do not spare reputation in this."

sentences.zh: 」因再稱疾求罷，帝溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: He again cited illness and asked to leave; the emperor issued a mild edict comforting him and retaining him.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to retire citing illness; the emperor comforted him and kept him.

sentences.zh: 而給事中郭允厚、郭興治復相繼詆元標甚力。

translations.literal: But Supervising Secretaries Guo Yunhou and Guo Xingzhi again in succession attacked Yuanbiao with great force.
translations.idiomatic: But Guo Yunhou and Guo Xingzhi attacked Yuanbiao again with great force.

sentences.zh: 從吾又上言：「臣壯歲登朝，即與楊起元、孟化鯉、陶望齡輩立講學會，自臣告歸乃廢。

translations.literal: Congwu again memorialized: "When your servant in his vigorous years entered court, he at once with Yang Qiyuan, Meng Huayu, Tao Wangling, and others established a lecture society; after your servant asked to return home it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Congwu memorialized again: "In my vigorous years I entered court and with Yang Qiyuan, Meng Huayu, and Tao Wangling founded a lecture society; after I retired it lapsed.

sentences.zh: 京師講學，昔已有之，何至今日遂為詬厲？

translations.literal: Lecturing in the capital existed in former times—how can it today suddenly become a term of abuse?
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing in the capital is nothing new—how has it become abuse overnight?

sentences.zh: 」因再疏引歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted another memorial asking to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 四年春，起南京右都御史，累辭未上，召拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he was raised Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief; he repeatedly declined and did not go up; he was summoned as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he was made Nanjing right censor-in-chief but repeatedly declined; he was then summoned as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 會趙南星、高攀龍相繼去國，連疏力辭，予致仕。

translations.literal: When Zhao Nanxing and Gao Panlong left office in succession, he submitted successive memorials strenuously asking to leave and was granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Nanxing and Gao Panlong left in succession, he repeatedly begged to retire and was granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，魏忠賢黨張訥疏詆從吾，削籍。

translations.literal: The next autumn Wei Zhongxian's partisan Zhang Na memorialized to denounce Congwu, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Zhang Na, a partisan of Wei Zhongxian, denounced Congwu and had him struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 鄉人王紹徽素銜從吾，及為吏部，使喬應甲撫陜，捃摭百方，無所得。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Wang Shaohui had long borne a grudge against Congwu; when he became Minister of Personnel he had Qiao Yingjia grand-coordinate Shaanxi and gather evidence by every means, yet obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaohui, a fellow townsman, had long resented Congwu; as minister of personnel he sent Qiao Yingjia to Shaanxi to gather evidence by every means and found nothing.

sentences.zh: 乃毀書院，曳先聖像，擲之城隅。

translations.literal: Thereupon they destroyed the academy, dragged the image of the former sage, and threw it in a corner of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: They destroyed the academy, dragged off the sage's image, and flung it by the city wall.

sentences.zh: 從吾不勝憤悒，得疾卒。

translations.literal: Congwu could not bear the anger and distress; he took ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Congwu could not bear the outrage; he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官，贈太子太保，謚恭定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen his office was restored; he was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent with the posthumous name Gongding.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：趙南星諸人，持名檢，勵風節，嚴氣正性，侃侃立朝，天下望之如泰山喬嶽。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Zhao Nanxing and the others held to name and restraint, encouraged moral conduct, were stern in spirit and upright in nature, and stood at court with firm integrity; the realm looked to them as to Mount Tai or a lofty peak.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Zhao Nanxing and his fellows upheld integrity, encouraged moral conduct, and stood at court with unbending rectitude; the realm looked to them as to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 《詩》有之，「邦之司直」，其斯人謂歟？

translations.literal: The 《Odes》 has it, "the state's upright judge"—can this refer to such men?
translations.idiomatic: The 《Odes》 says, "the state's upright judge"—was it not men such as these?

sentences.zh: 權枉盈廷，譴謫相繼，「人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁」，悲夫！

translations.literal: Power bent and filled the court; censure and banishment followed one after another—"when men depart, the state is wasted"—how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Power bent and filled the court; punishment followed punishment—"when worthy men depart, the state wastes away"—how lamentable!
